[Murdifin] was read with the d (dal) both pronounced with a kasra and with a fatha. It was said: the meaning is that they are a reinforcement (ridf) for you.

If it is said: here He mentioned that He reinforced them with a thousand, while in (Surat Al 'Imran) He said: ﴿When you said to the believers, "Is it not enough for you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down? How then is the reconciliation between the two?

It is said: the scholars have differed regarding this reinforcement of three thousand and that of five thousand, into two opinions:

The first: that it was on the Day of Uhud, and it was a reinforcement conditional upon a condition; when the condition was not fulfilled, the reinforcement was cancelled. This is the view of al-Dahhak and Muqatil, and one of the two narrations from 'Ikrimah.

The second: that it was on the Day of Badr. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah.

The other narration from 'Ikrimah, and a group of exegetes chose it. The proof of these is that the context indicates this, for He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr when you were weak. So fear Allah that you may be grateful. When you said to the believers, "Is it not enough for you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down? Yes, if you are steadfast and godfearing"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 123-125], up to His saying: ﴿And Allah did not make it [this reinforcement] except as good news for you and that your hearts might be assured thereby﴾ [Al 'Imran: 126]. These said: when they sought help, He reinforced them with the complete three thousand, then He reinforced them with the complete five thousand when they were steadfast and godfearing. So this gradation and the continuity of reinforcement had a better effect, was stronger for their souls, and more gladdening to them than that it came once. It is like the continuity of revelation and its descent time after time.

It was said in its interpretation: "Strengthen their hearts, and give them good news of victory."

And it was said: "Be present with them in the fighting."

Both sayings are true, for they were present with them in the fighting and strengthened their hearts.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 8, verse 17 (part 1 of 2):

As for His saying, ﴿You did not throw when you threw, but God threw﴾, what is meant is the handful of pebbles that he (ﷺ) threw at the faces of the polytheists, which reached the eyes of all of them. God, glorified is He, attributed the throwing to him in terms of the casting and tossing, since he did it, and negated it from him in terms of its reaching all the polytheists. This is the act of the Lord, exalted is He, which the power of a servant cannot reach. The word ramy (throwing) is applied to flinging (khadhf), which is its beginning, and to reaching the target (iyṣāl), which is its end.

As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and that He might test the believers with a good trial from Him﴾, the "good trial" here is the blessing of victory, booty, and triumph over the enemies. It is not from ibtilā' (testing) in the sense of examination with what is disliked. Rather, it is from abla-hu balā'an ḥasanan (He bestowed upon him a good favour) when He bestows a blessing upon him. It is said: ablāka Allāh (God has favoured you), not ibtalāka (God has tested you). So He favoured him with good, and tested him with hardships, typically, as in the hadith: "Indeed I will test you and I will test [others] for your sake."

(Section)
I say: A group believed that the meaning of the verse is the negation of the Messenger's act from him and its attribution to the Lord, exalted is He. They made this a foundation for jabr (determinism) and for denying that actions are attributed to servants, and for affirming that they are attributed to the Lord alone. This is a grave error on their part in understanding the Qur'an. For if that were correct, it would have to be applied to all deeds. It would be said: "You did not pray when you prayed, you did not fast when you fasted, you did not sacrifice when you sacrificed, and you did not perform any act when you performed it, but God did that." If they applied this generally, it would apply to all the actions of servants, their acts of obedience and their acts of disobedience, since there is no difference. If they restricted it to the Messenger alone and all his acts, or to his throwing alone, they would be contradicting themselves. These people were not granted success in understanding what the verse intends.

Furthermore: this verse was revealed concerning his (ﷺ) throwing at the polytheists on the Day of Badr a handful of pebbles, and it did not leave the face of any one of them without striking it. It is known that such a throw by a human does not reach this extent. So from him (ﷺ) came the beginning of the throwing, which is the flinging, and from God, glorified and exalted is He, came its completion, which is the reaching of the target. Thus He attributed to him the throwing of flinging, which is its beginning, and negated from him the throwing of reaching, which is its end.

A parallel to this is His saying in the same verse: ﴿So you did not kill them, but God killed them﴾, then He said: ﴿You did not throw when you threw, but God threw﴾. He informed them that He alone was the one who singularly killed them, and that this was not by you, just as He singularly delivered the pebbles into their eyes, and this was not from His Messenger. The point of the verse's allusion is that He, glorified is He, established apparent causes for repelling the polytheists, but He undertook their repulsion and destruction by hidden causes other than those that appear to people. So what occurred of defeat, killing, and victory was attributed to Him, and through Him, and He is the best of helpers.

(Section)
Abu Jahl sought victory on that day, saying: "O God, whichever of us is more severed from the ties of kinship and brings what we do not know, destroy him tomorrow morning. O God, whichever of us is more beloved to You and more pleasing to You, give him victory today." God, mighty and majestic is He, then revealed: ﴿If you seek a decision, the decision has indeed come to you; and if you desist, it is better for you; and if you return, We will return; and your company will avail you nothing, however numerous it be; and that God is with the believers﴾ [al-Anfal: 19].

When the Muslims set their hands upon the enemy, killing and taking prisoners, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh was standing at the door of the tent in which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was, which was the 'arīsh (a shelter), girded with a sword among some of the Helpers. "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) saw in the face of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh aversion to what the people were doing, so the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'It seems you dislike what the people are doing?' He said: 'Indeed, by God, it was the first battle God caused among the polytheists, and a thorough slaughter in killing was dearer to me than sparing the men.'"

When the fighting cooled and the people turned to flee in defeat, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Who will look for us what Abu Jahl did?" Ibn Mas'ud set out and found him, struck by the two sons of 'Afra' until he was cold dead. He took hold of his beard and said: "Are you Abu Jahl?" He said: "To whom does the victory belong today?" He said: "To God and to His Messenger. Has God disgraced you, O enemy of God?" He said: "Is there anything above a man whom his own people have killed?" Then Abdullah killed him, and then came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I have killed him." He said: "God, there is no god but He," and he repeated it three times. Then he said: "God is greatest, praise belongs to God who fulfilled His promise, supported His servant, and defeated the confederates alone. Come, show me him." So we went and I showed him to him, and he said: "This is the Pharaoh of this nation."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 8, verse 17 (part 2 of 2):

Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf took Umayyah ibn Khalaf and his son Ali as captives. Bilal saw him, and Umayyah had been torturing him in Makkah. So he said: "The head of disbelief, Umayyah ibn Khalaf! I will not be saved if he is saved!" Then he called out to a group of the Ansar, and Abd al-Rahman, running with the two of them, tried to protect them from them. They caught up with them, and [the Ansar] were occupied with his son instead of Umayyah, so they finished with him. Then they caught up with the two of them. Abd al-Rahman said to him: "Kneel down." He knelt, and he threw himself over him, and they struck him with swords from beneath him until they killed him. Some of the swords struck the leg of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. Before that, Umayyah had said to him: "Who is the man marked on his chest with an ostrich feather?" He said: "That is Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib." Umayyah said: "That is the one who did the terrible things to us." Abd al-Rahman had with him some armour that he had taken as spoils. When Umayyah saw him, he said to him: "I am better for you than this armour." So he threw it down and [Abd al-Rahman] took him. When the Ansar killed him, [Umayyah] used to say: "May Allah have mercy on Bilal; he has bereaved me of my armour and my captive."

On that day the sword of Ukkashah ibn Mihsan broke, so the Prophet ﷺ gave him a piece of firewood and said: "Take this." When Ukkashah took it and brandished it, it became in his hand a long, strong, white sword. He kept fighting with it until he was killed in the Ridda (apostasy wars) during the days of Abu Bakr.

Al-Zubayr met Ubaydah ibn Saeed ibn al-As, who was fully armoured, so that nothing of him could be seen except his eyes. Al-Zubayr charged at him with his spear and stabbed him in the eye, and he died. He then placed his foot on the spear and pulled, and it was with great effort that he removed it, its two ends having bent. Urwah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked him for it, and he gave it to him. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken [in death], [al-Zubayr] took it back. Then Abu Bakr asked for it, and he gave it to him. When Abu Bakr died, Umar asked him for it, and he gave it to him. When Umar died, he took it back. Then Uthman asked for it, and he gave it to him. When Uthman died, it fell into the possession of the family of Ali. Then Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr asked for it, and it remained with him until he was killed.

Rifa'ah ibn Rafi said: "I was struck by an arrow on the day of Badr and my eye was gouged out. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spat into it and supplicated for me, and nothing ever harmed me from it."

When the battle was over, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and stood over the dead and said: "What an evil clan of the Prophet you were to your Prophet! You denied me while people believed me, you forsook me while people supported me, and you expelled me while people sheltered me."

Then he ordered that they be dragged to one of the wells of Badr, and they were thrown into it. Then he stood over them and said: "O Utbah ibn Rabiah, O Shaybah ibn Rabiah, O so-and-so, O so-and-so, have you found what your Lord promised you to be true? For I have found what my Lord promised me to be true." Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "O Messenger of Allah, why do you address people who have already decomposed?" He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, you are not more able to hear what I say than they are, but they cannot answer." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained at the battlefield for three days, for when he prevailed over a people he would remain on their ground for three days.

Then he departed, aided and victorious, his eyes comforted by Allah's help to him, and with him were the captives and the spoils. When he was at al-Safra, he divided the spoils and struck off the neck of al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn Kaladah. Then, when he halted at Irq al-Zabyah, he struck off the neck of Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt.

The Prophet ﷺ entered Madinah aided, victorious and supported, and every enemy who was in and around Madinah feared him. Then a great many of the people of Madinah embraced Islam, and at that time Abd Allah ibn Ubayy the hypocrite and his companions outwardly entered Islam.

The Lord, glorified is He, informed that their place does not accept His blessing. Along with this lack of acceptance, there is another obstacle preventing it from reaching them: their turning away and aversion when they recognize it and verify it.

It should be known that the causes of abandonment (khudhlan) are the soul remaining as it was originally created and being neglected and left to itself. So the causes of abandonment come from it and within it. The causes of success (tawfiq) are that God, glorified is He, made the soul receptive to blessing. So the causes of success come from Him and from His grace, for He is the Creator of this and that, just as He created parts of the earth, some receptive to plants and others not receptive to them. He created trees, some that bear fruit and others that do not. He created the bee receptive to producing from its belly a drink of varying colors, while the wasp is not receptive to that. He created good spirits receptive to His remembrance, thanks, love, glorification, magnification, unification, and advising His servants. He created wicked spirits not receptive to that, but to its opposite. He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.

(Benefit)

He, glorified is He, informed that He cut off from them the source of guidance, which is making their hearts hear and understand what benefits them, because the place does not accept it, for there is no good in it. A person only submits to the truth through the good within him: his inclination toward it, his seeking it, his love for it, his eagerness for it, and his joy at attaining it. These people have none of that in their hearts. So guidance reached them and fell upon them, as rain descending from the sky falls upon hard, elevated land that holds no water and grows no herbage. It is neither receptive to water nor to plants. Water in itself is mercy and life, but there is no receptivity to it in that land.

Then God affirmed this meaning regarding them in His saying: ﴿And had He made them hear, they would have turned away while being averse﴾ [al-Anfal: 23].

He informed that in them, along with the lack of acceptance and understanding, there is another affliction, which is arrogance, aversion, and corrupted intention. Had they understood, they would not have submitted, nor followed the truth, nor acted upon it. So guidance regarding these people is the guidance of clarification and establishing proof, not the guidance of success and direction. Thus guidance did not connect with mercy for them.

If it is said: He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them hear﴾. This implies that there is no receptivity in them and no good with them at all. If there were, they would have been brought out of the Fire along with the monotheists, for He brings out of the Fire whoever has in his heart even the least, least, least weight of a mustard seed of good. So it is known that these people do not have this small amount of good?

It is said: The good in this hadith is faith in God and His messengers, as in the other wording, "even the least, least, least weight of faith." It is affirming His messengers and submitting to them with the heart and the limbs. As for the good in the verse, what is meant is acceptance, purity, and recognition of the measure of blessing and thanks to the Bestower of it. So if God, glorified is He, had known that in them, He would have made them hear in a way that benefits them. For they heard a hearing by which proof was established against them. Yet that receptivity's effect has gone and been nullified by disbelief and denial, and it became like a nonexistent thing that benefits no one. Its effect appeared only in the establishment of proof against them, not in their benefiting from what they did and were certain of.

(Section)

The twenty-first category: His, glorified is He, informing about His leaving some of what is within His power because of the corruption it would entail, and that the benefit lies in leaving it. If the matter returned merely to pure will, that would not be a cause for the ruling. Like His saying: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in Allah's sight are the deaf and the dumb who do not reason. And had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And had He made them hear, they would have turned away while being averse﴾ [al-Anfal: 22–23]. He explained the withholding of the hearing by which they would benefit, which is the hearing of understanding, by the fact that there is no good in them that would make it fitting for Him to make them hear. And He explained it by the presence in them of another obstacle that prevents benefiting from what is heard, even if they heard it, namely arrogance and aversion. This is valid only for one who commands, forbids, and acts for rulings and benefits. As for one who strips his act of that, the absence of a ruling is attributed only to the bare absence of its causer.

From this is His declaring Himself free of much that He is able to do, so He does not do it because it contradicts His wisdom and praiseworthiness. And His saying: ﴿Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ [al-Anfal: 33]. And His saying: ﴿Allah would not misguide a people after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should avoid; indeed Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ [al-Tawba: 115]. And His saying: ﴿Your Lord would not destroy the towns unjustly while their people are reformers﴾ [Hud: 117]. And His saying: ﴿Your Lord would not destroy the towns until He sends in their mother [town] a messenger reciting to them Our verses. And We would not destroy the towns unless their people were wrongdoers﴾ [al-Qasas: 59]. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And had He made them hear, they would have turned away while being averse﴾ [al-Anfal: 23].

He also said: ﴿The blind and the seeing are not alike, nor are darknesses and light, nor shade and scorching heat. Nor are the living and the dead alike. The level of hearing revolves around conveying the intended purpose of the address to the heart, and from this hearing follows the hearing of acceptance.

So there are three levels: the hearing of the ear, the hearing of the heart, and the hearing of acceptance and response.

The difference between this level and the level of understanding is that this level is attained only through the ear, while the level of understanding is more general. So in this respect it is more specific than the level of understanding, while in another respect the level of understanding is more specific: it relates to the intended meaning, its necessary implications, its connections, and its indications. The level of hearing revolves around conveying the intended purpose of the address to the heart, and from this hearing follows the hearing of acceptance.

So there are three levels: the hearing of the ear, the hearing of the heart, and the hearing of acceptance and response.

Thus Allah, glorified and exalted, informs us that our life lies in what Allah and the Messenger call us to of knowledge and faith. So it is known that the death and ruin of the heart come from the loss of that.

Allah, glorified, has likened those who do not respond to His Messenger to the people of the graves. This is one of the finest of comparisons, for their bodies are graves for their hearts. Their hearts have died and been buried within their bodies. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah makes hear whom He wills, and you cannot make hear those who are in the graves﴾ [Fatir: 22].

The poet has spoken well:

*Ignorance before death is a death for its people,*
*and their bodies, before the graves, are graves.*

*Their spirits are in loneliness away from their bodies,*
*and for them there is no resurrection until the Resurrection.*

For this reason Allah, glorified, made the revelation He sends down to the prophets a spirit, as He said, exalted: ﴿He casts the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [Ghafir: 15], in two places in His Book, and He said: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit from Our command﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. This is because the life of spirits and hearts is through it. This good life is the one with which Allah, glorified, singled out whoever accepted His revelation and acted upon it, when He said:

﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do﴾ [al-Nahl: 97].

So Allah, glorified and exalted, singled them out with a good life in both abodes.

**(Section)**

This verse contains several matters.

The first: beneficial life is attained only through responding to Allah and His Messenger. Whoever does not attain this response has no life, even if he has animal life, which he shares with the basest of animals. True, good life is the life of one who responds to Allah and His Messenger outwardly and inwardly. These are the living, even if they die, and others are dead, even if their bodies are alive. For this reason, the most complete of people in life are the most complete in responding to the call of the Messenger (ﷺ).

Every call he made contains life. Whoever misses a part of it misses a part of life, and in it there is life in proportion to what one responds to the Messenger.

Mujahid said: "li-ma yuhyikum" means: for the truth.

Qatadah said: it is this Qur'an; in it is life, trust, salvation and protection in this world and the Hereafter. Al-Suddi said: it is Islam, by which He gave them life after their death through disbelief.

Ibn Ishaq and Urwah ibn al-Zubayr said, and the wording is his: "li-ma yuhyikum" means: for the war through which Allah honoured you after humiliation, strengthened you after weakness, and protected you through it from your enemy after they had subdued you.

All of these are expressions of one reality, namely standing by what the Messenger brought, outwardly and inwardly.

Al-Wahidi said: most of them hold that the meaning of His words "li-ma yuhyikum" is jihad. This is the view of Ibn Ishaq and the choice of most of the scholars of meanings.

Al-Farra' said: when He calls you to the revival of your affair through fighting your enemy, meaning that their affair is only strengthened by war and jihad. So if they abandon jihad, their affair weakens and their enemy becomes bold against them.

I say: jihad is among the greatest things by which they are given life, in this world, in the barzakh (the intermediate state), and in the Hereafter. As for this world, their strength and their subjugation of their enemy come through jihad.

As for the barzakh, Allah, exalted, said: ﴿And do not think of those who have been killed in the cause of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision﴾.

As for the Hereafter, the share of the mujahidun and the martyrs of its life and bliss is greater than the share of others. For this reason Ibn Qutaybah said: "li-ma yuhyikum" means martyrdom.

Some exegetes said: "li-ma yuhyikum" means Paradise, for it is the abode of life, and in it is lasting, good life. This was related by Abu Ali al-Jurjani. The verse encompasses all of this, for faith, Islam, the Qur'an and jihad give life to the hearts with a good life, and the perfection of life is in Paradise. The Messenger calls to faith and to Paradise; he calls to life in this world and in the Hereafter.

A human being is in need of two kinds of life: the life of his body, by which he perceives what benefits and harms him and prefers what benefits him over what harms him. When this life is diminished in him, pain and weakness increase accordingly. This is why the life of the sick, the grieved, the anxious, the one plagued by worry, fear, poverty and humiliation is less than the life of one who is free from these.

And the life of his heart and spirit, by which he distinguishes truth from falsehood, error from right guidance, and desire from misguidance, so that he chooses the truth over its opposite. This life gives him the power to distinguish between what benefits and what harms in knowledge, wills and deeds. It also gives him strength of faith, will and love of the truth, and strength of hatred and aversion to falsehood. So his perception, discernment and support of the truth are in proportion to his share of this life.

Just as a living body has a fuller sense and feeling of what benefits and what pains, and its inclination toward what benefits and its aversion to what pains is greater, this is according to the life of the body; and that is according to the life of the heart. When its life is nullified, its discernment is nullified. If it has some degree of discernment, it lacks the strength by which it prefers what benefits over what harms. Just as a human being has no life until the angel, who is the messenger of Allah, breathes into him of His spirit, so he becomes alive by that breathing. And the one who lacks it is among the dead. Likewise, his spirit and heart have no life until the Messenger (ﷺ) breathes into them of the Spirit that Allah has cast upon him. Allah said: ﴿He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾, and He said: ﴿He casts the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾.

And He said: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit from Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor faith; but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants﴾.

So He informed that His revelation is a spirit and a light.

Life and illumination depend on the breathing of the Messenger in the angelic manner. Whoever receives the angelic breathing and the human breathing of the Messenger attains both lives. Whoever receives the angelic breathing without the breathing of the Messenger attains one of the two lives and misses the other.

Allah, exalted, said: ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one whose likeness is in darkness, never to emerge from it?﴾

So He combined for him light and life, just as He combined death and darkness for the one who turns away from His Book. Ibn Abbas and all the exegetes said: he was a disbeliever, astray, and We guided him.

His words: ﴿and made for him a light by which he walks among the people﴾ contain several matters.

The first: he walks among the people with light while they are in darkness. His likeness and theirs is like people over whom the night has darkened, so they went astray and did not find the way. Another person has with him a light by which he walks on the path, sees it, and sees what he should beware of in it.

The second: he walks by his light, and they borrow from it, since they need light.

The third: he walks by his light on the Day of Resurrection over the Sirat (the bridge over Hell), when the people of polytheism and hypocrisy remain in the darkness of their shirk and hypocrisy.

His words: ﴿And know that Allah comes between a person and his heart﴾.

The well-known understanding of the verse is that He comes between the believer and disbelief, and between the disbeliever and faith. He comes between those who obey Him and their disobedience, and between those who disobey Him and their obedience.

This is the view of Ibn Abbas and the majority of the exegetes. There is another view in the verse: that the meaning is that He, glorified, is near to his heart, nothing of it hidden from Him. So He is between him and his heart. This was mentioned by al-Wahidi from Qatadah.

This view is more fitting to the context, because response originates in the heart, so response of the body without the heart does not benefit.

Indeed Allah, glorified, is between the servant and his heart. He knows whether his heart responded to Him, and whether he concealed that or concealed its opposite.

According to the first view, the connection is: if you are sluggish in responding and delay in it, then do not feel secure that Allah may come between you and your hearts, so that you are no longer enabled to respond afterward, as a punishment for abandoning it after the truth has become clear and evident. This is like His words: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sight away, as they did not believe in it the first time﴾, and His words: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah turned their hearts away﴾, and His words: ﴿They would not have believed in what they had already denied before﴾.

So the verse contains a warning against abandoning response in the heart, even if one responds with the limbs.

The verse also contains another secret: He combined for them the Law and the command to it, which is response, and the divine decree and faith in it. It is like His words: ﴿For whoever among you wills to take the straight path. But you do not will, except that Allah wills, Lord of the worlds﴾, and His words: ﴿So whoever wills may remember it. And they will not remember unless Allah wills﴾.

And Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 8, verse 29 (part 1 of 2):

Al-furqan is honour and victory, salvation and the light that distinguishes between truth and falsehood.

[Section: It is fitting for the mufti to invoke Allah often for himself for success (tawfiq)]

It is fitting for the mufti to invoke often the sound hadith: "O Allah, Lord of Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differ. Guide me, by Your permission, to the truth regarding that over which they have differed, for You guide whom You will to a straight path." Our shaykh used to invoke much with this, and whenever matters became difficult for him he would say: "O Teacher of Ibrahim, teach me."

He also often sought help with this, following the example of Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, when he said to Malik ibn Yakhamir al-Saksaki at his death, seeing him weeping: "By Allah, I am not weeping over worldly things I used to obtain from you, but I am weeping over the knowledge and faith which I used to learn from you." Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Indeed knowledge and faith have their place; whoever seeks them finds them. Seek knowledge from four: from 'Uwaymir Abu al-Darda', from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari," and he mentioned the fourth. "If these cannot master it, then all the people of the earth are even less capable of it. So hold to the Teacher of Ibrahim, may the blessings of Allah be upon him."

Some of the early generation (salaf) used to say when giving a fatwa: "Glory be to You, we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed You are the All-Knowing, the All-Wise."

Makhul used to say: "There is no power and no strength except with Allah." Malik used to say: "What Allah wills. There is no power except with Allah, the Most High, the Mighty." Some of them used to say: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast (25), and ease my task for me (26), and loosen a knot from my tongue (27), that they may understand my speech (28)﴾.

Some of them used to say: "O Allah, grant me success, guide me, make me upright, combine for me correctness with reward, and protect me from error and deprivation."

Some of them used to recite al-Fatiha, and we have tested this ourselves and found it to be the strongest means of attaining correctness.

All of this rests upon good intention, sincerity of purpose, and true orientation in seeking aid from the First Teacher, the Teacher of the messengers and prophets, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all. For he who sincerely turns to Him, seeking to convey His religion, guide His servants, advise them, and avoid speaking about Him without knowledge, will not be turned away. When his intention and desire in this are sound, he will not lack a reward, even if he misses the two rewards. And Allah is the One sought for help.

Imam Ahmad was asked: "At times the matter becomes difficult for us from your side; whom should we ask after you?" He said: "Ask Abd al-Wahhab al-Warraq, for he is deserving of being granted correctness."

Imam Ahmad followed the saying of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him: "Draw near to the mouths of the obedient and listen to what they say, for matters of truth are revealed to them, because their hearts are close to Allah. Whenever the heart draws near to Allah, the obstacles of evil depart from it, and the light of its unveiling of truth becomes more complete and stronger; and whenever it moves away from Allah, obstacles multiply upon it and the light of its unveiling of what is correct weakens. For knowledge is a light which Allah casts into the heart, by which the servant distinguishes between error and correctness."

Malik said to al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with both of them, at the first time he met him: "I see that Allah has cast a light into your heart, so do not extinguish it with the darkness of disobedience." And the Exalted has said: ﴿O you who believe, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion (furqan)﴾ [al-Anfal: 29].

Among al-furqan is the light by which the servant distinguishes between truth and falsehood. Whenever his heart is closer to Allah, his furqan is more complete. And success is from Allah.

[Section: Al-Furuq al-Tul (the extended distinctions)]

This is one of the extended distinctions. Perhaps, if destiny aids, we shall devote to it a great book; what we have mentioned is only to alert to its principles, and the intelligent person will suffice with some of it. The whole religion is distinction (furq), and the Book of Allah is the criterion (furqan) of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace; it distinguishes between people. Whoever fears Allah, Allah will grant him a criterion: ﴿O you who believe, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion﴾.

The day of Badr was named the Day of the Criterion because it distinguished between the friends of Allah and His enemies. All guidance is criterion, while misguidance has as its root conjunction, just as the polytheists combined the worship of Allah with the worship of idols, and His love with the love of idols, and what He loves and is pleased with with what He decreed and decided. They made the matter one, and they argued from His decree and destiny to His love and pleasure. They combined usury with trade, saying: "Trade is only like usury." They combined the slaughtered animal with the carrion, saying: "How do we eat what we kill but not what Allah kills?" Those who had departed from the laws combined the lawful and the unlawful, saying: "This woman Allah created, and that one He created; this animal He created, and that one He created; how then is this permitted and that forbidden?" They combined the friends of the Merciful with the friends of Satan. A group of the Unificationists (al-Ittihadiyya) came and levelled the valley with the villages, gathering everything into one essence, and said: "It is Allah, there is no god but He." The author of their Fusus and the framer of their texts said: "Know that the matter is a Qur'an, not a furqan":

"The matter is nothing but one uniform order, in which there is no praise nor blame,
And happiness has only been specified, while nature and the Lawgiver hold the judgement."

The point is that people of insight are the possessors of the furqan, and the one with the greatest furqan among the ambiguous matters is the greatest in insight. Ambiguity occurs in statements, actions, states, wealth and men, and most of the people of knowledge have fallen into ambiguities in all of these. The criterion is not attained except by a light which Allah casts into the heart of whomever He wills of His servants, by which he sees the realities of matters in its illumination and distinguishes their truth from their falsehood, their soundness from their corruption: ﴿And whoever Allah does not give light, for him there is no light﴾.

Do not consider this section lengthy, for it is perhaps one of the most beneficial sections of the book, and the need for it is great. If Allah grants you insight in it, you will come out of it to a greater criterion than it: the distinction between the monotheism of the messengers and the monotheism of the denuders (mu'attilun); the distinction between the affirmation of attributes, the Highness and the speech of Allah in reality, and between likening and assimilation (tashbih and tamthil); the distinction between pure practical volitional tawhid and the diminishing of those of rank in their ranks which Allah has assigned to them; the distinction between pure following of the infallible and turning to other than it; the distinction between taking a scholar as an authority and benefiting from the light of his knowledge and seeking aid through his understanding; the distinction between the friends of the Merciful and the friends of Satan; the distinction between the state of faith and mercy, the satanic disbelieving state, and the soul's state; and the distinction between the judgement revealed, binding upon each one, and the interpreted judgement which one fears to be permissible to follow only in necessity, with no blame on its opponent.

[Section]

We conclude the book with a subtle indication of the differences between these matters, since each distinction requires a great book to expand it. The distinction between the monotheism of the messengers and the monotheism of the denuders is that the monotheism of the messengers is the affirmation of the attributes of perfection for Allah in detail, and the worship of Him alone without partner, so one does not make for Him a rival in intention, love, fear, hope, speech, oath or vow; rather the servant removes rivals from his heart, intention, tongue and worship, just as they are non-existent in reality, having no existence whatsoever, so he does not grant them existence in his heart or tongue.

As for the monotheism of the denuders, it is the negation of the realities of His names and attributes and their denudation. Whoever among them is able to denude them from his tongue does so: he does not mention them, nor any verse containing them, nor any hadith explicitly stating any of them. Whoever cannot prevent the mention of them assaults them by distortion, negates their reality, and makes them mere active names without meaning, or their meaning is of the kind of riddles and puzzles. Moreover, whoever among them consistently pursues denudation knows that what he has turned the text toward in meaning necessarily entails the same thing he fled from; if it entails likeness or resemblance or created-ness in reality, it entails it in the meaning to which the text was turned, and if it does not entail it in this, it is more fitting that it not entail it in reality. Having known this, he cannot but denude all of it. This is the consistent pursuit of the root of denudation, and the distinction is closer to it, but it is self-contradictory, arbitrarily judging by falsehood, since Allah affirmed some of what He affirmed for Himself and negated the other part; the false implication in both is one, and the true implication does not separate between them.

The point is that they called this denudation "monotheism", while it is in fact heresy (ilhad) regarding the names and attributes of the Lord, Exalted, and denudation of their realities.

[Section: The distinction between the glorification (tanzih) of the messengers and the glorification of the denuders]

The distinction between the glorification of the messengers and the glorification of the denuders is that the messengers glorified Him, glory be to Him, from the deficiencies and defects from which He glorified Himself, those which contradict His perfection and the perfection of His lordship and greatness: such as drowsiness, sleep, heedlessness, death, weariness and injustice; and His having desires; and being named with a partner, a consort, a helper, a child, or an intercessor without His permission; and that He should leave His servants neglected and purposeless; or that their creation should be in vain; or that the creation of the heavens and earth and what is between them should be void, without reward, punishment, command or prohibition; or that He should equate between His friends and His enemies, between the righteous and the wicked, between the disbelievers and the believers; or that there should be in His dominion what He does not will; or that He should need another in any way; or that another should have any share of command with Him; or that forgetfulness, inattention or oblivion should be ascribed to Him; or that He should break His promise, change His words, or that evil should be attributed to Him, whether by name, attribute or act. Rather, all His names are most beautiful, all His attributes are perfection, and all His acts are good, wise and beneficial. This is the glorification of the messengers of their Lord.

As for the denuders, they glorified Him from what He described Himself with of perfection: they glorified Him from speaking or being spoken to by anyone; they glorified Him from being established on His Throne, from hands being raised to Him, from good words ascending to Him, from anything descending from Him, from the angels and the Spirit ascending to Him, and from being above His servants and above all His creation, high above them; they glorified Him from holding the heavens in His hand and the earth in His other hand, from holding the heavens upon a finger, the earth upon a finger, the mountains upon a finger, and the trees upon a finger; they glorified Him from having a face that the believers see with their eyes in Paradise, from speaking to them and greeting them, from manifesting Himself to them laughing, and from descending every night to the lowest heaven, saying: "Who will ask forgiveness of Me that I may forgive him? Who will ask of Me that I may give him?" So for them there is no descent and no speech. They glorified Him from doing anything for the sake of anything else; rather His acts are not for wisdom or for any intended purpose. They glorified Him from having complete will and executed volition; rather He wills a thing while His servants will its opposite, so what the servant wills happens rather than what the Lord wills, and He wills a thing that does not occur, and what He does not will occurs. They called this justice, just as they called that glorification monotheism. They glorified Him from loving or being loved, and from mercy, compassion, anger and pleasure. Others glorified Him from hearing and sight, others from knowledge, and others glorified Him from existence, saying: "What these glorifiers fled to from likeness and resemblance would entail upon us in existence, so we must glorify Him from it." This is the glorification of the heretics, while the first is the glorification of the messengers.

[Section: The distinction between affirming the realities of the names and attributes and likening and assimilation]

The distinction between affirming the realities of the names and attributes and likening and assimilation is what Imam Ahmad and those who agreed with him among the imams of guidance said: likening and assimilation is for you to say "a hand like my hand", or "a hearing like my hearing", or "a sight like my sight", and the like.

As for when you say "hearing, sight, hand, face, and establishment" which resembles none of the attributes of created beings, but rather the difference between one attribute and another is like the difference between one described thing and another, then what likening or assimilation is there here, were it not for the deception of the heretics? So the axis of truth, upon which the messengers agreed, is that Allah be described by what He described Himself with and what His Messenger described Him with, without distortion or denudation, and without likening or assimilation: affirmation of the attributes and negation of resemblance to created things. Whoever likens Allah to His creation has disbelieved; whoever denies the realities of what Allah described Himself with has disbelieved; and whoever affirms for Him the realities of the names and attributes while negating resemblance to created things has been guided to the straight path.

[Section: The distinction between the purification of tawhid and the diminishing of those of rank]

The distinction between the purification of tawhid and the diminishing of those of rank: the purification of tawhid is that one does not give a created being any of the right of the Creator or His distinctive features. So one does not worship, pray to, or prostrate to him; does not swear by his name; does not vow to him; does not rely upon him; does not deify him; does not swear by him against Allah; does not worship in order to draw near to Allah in rank; and does not equate him with the Lord of the worlds in the saying of one who says: "What Allah wills and you will", "This is from you and from Allah", "I am with Allah and with you", "I rely on Allah and on you", "Allah is for me in heaven and you on earth", "This is from your charity and Allah's charity", "I repent to Allah and to you", or "I am under the protection of Allah and of you."

Yet one prostrates to a created being as the polytheists prostrate to their shaykhs, shaves his head for him, swears by his name, vows to him, prostrates to his grave after death, seeks his aid in his needs and affairs, pleases him with the wrath of Allah and does not anger him for the pleasure of Allah, draws near to him more than he draws near to Allah, loves, fears and hopes in him more than he loves, fears and hopes in Allah, or equates him with Allah. When one diminishes the distinctive features of Lordship from a created being and places him in the position of a pure servant who does not own for himself any benefit, harm, death, life or resurrection, is this not a deprecation of him and a lowering of his rank? Even if the polytheists are enraged. And it is authentically reported from the master of the children of Adam, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, that he said:

"Do not exalt me as the Christians exalted the son of Mary, for I am only a servant; so say: 'the servant of Allah and His messenger.'"

He also said: "O people, I do not wish that you raise me above my station." He said: "Do not take my grave as a festival." He said: "O Allah, do not make my grave an idol that is worshipped." He said: "Do not say: 'What Allah wills and Muhammad wills.'" A man said to him: "What Allah wills and you will," and he said: "Have you made Allah a rival?" A man who had sinned said: "O Allah, I repent to You and do not repent to Muhammad," and he said: "He has recognised the truth for its people." And Allah the Exalted has said to him: ﴿You have no share in the affair﴾, and He said: ﴿Say: Indeed the whole affair belongs to Allah﴾, and He said: ﴿Say: I do not possess for myself any harm or benefit except what Allah wills﴾, and He said: ﴿Say: Indeed I do not possess for you harm or right guidance. Say: Indeed no one can protect me from Allah, nor will I find any refuge besides Him﴾ — meaning: I will not find anyone other than Him to whom I can resort and on whom I can rely. And he said to his daughter Fatimah, his paternal uncle al-Abbas, and his aunt Safiyya: "I do not possess anything for you against Allah." (1)

And in a wording in the Sahih: "I cannot avail you anything against Allah." (2)

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 8, verse 29 (part 2 of 2):

They found this grievous, the polytheists with their shaykhs and their gods, and they refused all of it, and they claimed for their shaykhs and their objects of worship the opposite of all this. They alleged that whoever deprived them of that had diminished their ranks and belittled them. Yet they themselves have utterly diminished and belittled the side of divinity, so they have a generous share of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when God alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink; but when those other than Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice.﴾

[Section: The difference between singling out the following of the Infallible (ﷺ) and dismissing and nullifying the statements of the scholars]

The difference between singling out the following of the Infallible (ﷺ) and dismissing and nullifying the statements of the scholars is this: singling out the following means that you do not put forward, over what he brought, the statement or opinion of anyone, whoever he may be. Rather, you examine the soundness of the hadith.

First: if it is authenticated for you, then you examine its meaning.

Second: if its meaning becomes clear to you, you do not turn away from it, even if everyone from east to west opposes you. Far be it from God that the Community should agree upon opposing what its Prophet brought. Rather, there must be someone in the Community who has said it, even if you do not know him. So do not make your ignorance of the one who said it a proof against God and His Messenger. Rather, go to the text and do not weaken. Know that someone has certainly said it, but it has not reached you. This is while preserving the ranks of the scholars, loving them, believing in their sanctity and trustworthiness, and their striving to preserve and master the religion. They are circling between a reward and two rewards, and forgiveness. But this does not require dismissing the texts and preferring the statement of one of them over them on the pretext that he knows them better than you.

If that is so, then whoever goes to the text, knowing it better than you, why do you not agree with him, if you are truthful? Whoever presents the statements of the scholars to the texts, weighing them by the texts, and rejects those that contradict the text, has not dismissed their statements nor diminished their standing; rather, he has followed them, for they all commanded this. So the true follower of them is one who complies with what they enjoined, not one who opposes them in a statement that the text has contradicted. Opposing them in a particular statement is easier than opposing them in the overarching principle they commanded and called to, namely placing the text above their statements.

From here the difference becomes clear between imitating a scholar in everything he says, and seeking help from his understanding and illumination by the light of his knowledge. The first takes his statement without examining it or seeking its evidence from the Book and the Sunnah; rather, he makes it like a rope he puts around his neck and follows him by it, and that is why it is called taqlid (blind imitation). Unlike one who seeks help from his understanding and is illuminated by the light of his knowledge in reaching the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him. Such a person makes them like the first guide; once he reaches it, he is content with its guidance and has no need to rely on anything else. Whoever takes the star as a guide to the qibla, when he sees the qibla itself, his using the star has no further meaning. Al-Shafi'i said: The people have agreed that whoever has the Sunnah of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) made clear to him, it is not permissible for him to abandon it for anyone's statement.

[Section: The difference between the friends of the Merciful and the friends of Satan]

The difference between the friends of the Merciful and the friends of Satan: the friends of the Merciful: "No fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve." They are those who believed and were God-fearing.

They are those mentioned at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah up to His saying: "They are the successful." And in its middle, in His saying: "But righteousness is [in] one who believes in God and the Last Day..." up to His saying: "Those are the ones who are true, and those are the God-fearing."

And at the beginning of al-Anfal, up to His saying: "For them are degrees with their Lord and forgiveness and an honorable provision." And at the beginning of Surat al-Mu'minun, up to His saying: "They therein will abide forever." And at the end of Surat al-Furqan, and in His saying: "Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women..." to the end of the verse; and in His saying: "Unquestionably, the allies of God—no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve. Those who believed and were God-fearing." And in His saying: "And whoever obeys God and His Messenger and fears God and keeps his duty to Him—it is those who are the attainers of success." And in His saying: "Except those who pray, who are constant in their prayer..." up to His saying: "in gardens, honored." And in His saying: "The repentant, the worshippers, the praisers..." to the end of the verse.

So the friends of the Merciful are those sincere to their Lord, who judge by His Messenger in the sacred precinct and outside it, who oppose others for his Sunnah and do not oppose his ways for other than it. They do not innovate, nor call to innovation, nor take refuge in a group other than God, His Messenger and his Companions. They do not make their religion a pastime and a game, nor do they prefer the listening of Satan over the listening to the Qur'an, nor do they prefer the company of temptation over the pleasure of the Merciful, nor musical instruments and the oft-repeated over the seven oft-repeated (verses):

We have disavowed to God a people, with a sickness that brings a wasting disease,
And how often I said, "O people, you are on the brink of a precipice of listening to song,"
But when they scorned our warning, we left the deviator, and what he had done,
And would the deviator who makes song his habit respond to the caller to guidance?
So we lived upon the religion of the Chosen One, while they turned away from our path, and ours is good.

The friends of the Merciful are not confused with the friends of Satan except by one who lacks insight and faith. How could those who turn away from His Book and the guidance of His Messenger and his Sunnah, and who oppose it and turn to other than it, be His friends? They have bravely opposed it and deviated from the guidance and path of His Prophet: "They were not His friends; His friends are only the God-fearing, but most of them do not know."

So the friends of the Merciful are those who are clothed with what their Beloved loves, who call to it and wage war on those who depart from it. The friends of Satan are those who are clothed with what their beloved loves, in word and deed, call to it, and wage war on whoever forbids them from it. So when you see a man who loves satanic listening, the satanic caller to prayer, and the brothers of Satan, and calls to what Satan loves of polytheism, innovations and immorality, know that he is among his friends. If it is unclear to you, then test him in three places: his prayer, his love for the Sunnah and its people, and his aversion from those who oppose it, his calling to God and His messengers, and his singling out of monotheism and following and his establishing the Sunnah. Weigh him by that and do not weigh him by a state, nor a miraculous unveiling, nor a supernatural feat, even if he walks on water or flies in the air.

[Section: The difference between the state of faith and the satanic state]

By this the difference between the state of faith and the satanic state is known. The state of faith is the fruit of following the Messenger, sincerity in action, singling out monotheism, and the outcome of benefit to Muslims in their religion and their worldly life. It is only correct through steadfastness upon the Sunnah and adherence to the command and prohibition.

The satanic state is, in its nature, either polytheism or immorality. It arises from drawing near to the devils, connecting with them and resembling them. This state belongs to worshippers of idols, crosses, fires and Satan. When its possessor worships Satan, he is granted a state with which he hunts the weak in intellect and faith. "There is no god but God"—how many of creation have perished through these: "So that they might ruin them and confuse their religion for them. And had God willed, they would not have done it."

So every state whose possessor has departed from the judgment of the Book and what the Messenger brought is satanic, whatever it may be. I have heard of the states of sorcerers, fire-worshippers, cross-worshippers, and many who ascribe themselves to Islam outwardly while he is free of it in falsehood. He has a share of this state according to his allegiance to Satan and his enmity toward the Merciful. A man may be sincere, yet be deluded by his ignorance, so that his state is satanic despite asceticism, worship and sincerity; but the matter is not upon him, due to the paucity of his knowledge of the affairs of devils and angels and his ignorance of the realities of faith. These and those have related states, not of them, but a mere imitator, possessor of illusions and tricks. People have fallen into trouble through failing to distinguish between these and those, so they reckon every black thing a date and every white thing fat. The criterion (al-furqan) is the most precious thing in the world; it is a light God casts into the heart by which one distinguishes truth from falsehood and weighs the realities of affairs, their good and their evil, the righteous and the corrupt. Whoever lacks the criterion inevitably falls into associating with Satan. So God is the one sought for help, and upon Him is reliance.

[Section: The difference between the revealed judgment and the interpreted judgment]

The difference between the revealed judgment, which must be followed, and the interpreted judgment, whose ultimate status is that it may be followed: the revealed judgment is what God sent down upon a Messenger and judged by among His servants, and it is His judgment, with no judgment besides it.

As for the interpreted judgment, it consists of the differing opinions of the mujtahids, which need not be followed, and whoever opposes them is neither an unbeliever nor a sinner. For their proponents did not say, "This is the judgment of God and His Messenger," but said, "We have exerted ourselves by our own opinion; whoever wishes may accept it," and they did not oblige the Community to it. Abu Hanifa said, "This is my opinion; whoever brings us something better, we will accept it." Had it been the very judgment of God, it would not have been permissible for Abu Yusuf, Muhammad and others to oppose him in it. Likewise Malik, when al-Rashid asked him to compel the people to follow what is in the Muwatta', he refused and said: "The Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) scattered across the lands, and each people has what the others do not have."

Al-Shafi'i forbade his companions from following him and enjoined them to abandon his opinion when a hadith contradicted it. Imam Ahmad denounced those who wrote down his fatwas and compiled them, saying, "Do not imitate me, nor imitate so-and-so or so-and-so; take from where they took."

Had they, may God be pleased with them, known that their statements must be followed, they would have forbidden their companions to oppose them, and it would not have been permissible for their companions to issue rulings contrary to them on anything. Likewise, one of them would state an opinion and then issue a ruling contrary to it, so that two or three or more opinions are transmitted from him on a single question. Opinion and ijtihad, at their best, may be permissible to follow; the revealed judgment is not lawful for a Muslim to oppose or depart from.

As for the altered judgment, which is judging by other than what God has revealed, its execution is not lawful, nor is it permissible to follow it, and its doer is between disbelief, wickedness and wrongdoing.

The purpose is to draw attention to some states of the soul at peace (al-nafs al-mutma'innah), the blaming soul (al-nafs al-lawwamah) and the commanding soul (al-nafs al-ammarah), what these three souls share, what distinguishes some of them from others, the actions of each and their differences, aims and intentions. In this there is an indication of what has been transmitted: that it is one soul which is at times commanding, at times blaming, and at other times at peace. Most people are predominantly under the commanding soul. As for the soul at peace, it is the fewest of human souls in number and the greatest in rank before God, and it is the one to which it is said: "O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing. Enter among My servants, and enter My Garden."

And God, glorified and exalted, is the one asked, the one whose answering is hoped for, that He make our souls at peace in Him, devoted with their resolve to Him, fearing Him, desiring what is with Him; that He protect us from the evils of our souls and the misdeeds of our actions; and that He not make us among those whose hearts are heedless of His remembrance, who follow their desires and whose affair is excess, nor among "the greatest losers in deeds, those whose effort is lost in the life of this world while they think they are doing well in work."

Indeed He is the Hearer of supplication, the Object of hope, and He is sufficient for us and the best Disposer of affairs.

Ibn al-Qayyim, Commentary on the Qur'an (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim), on Surah 8, verse 33:

Reflect on the words of the Exalted to His Prophet: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them.﴾ How is it understood from this that if the presence of his body and person was among them, it removed the punishment from them, though they were his enemies? How much more so, then, is the presence of his secret (sirr), faith in him, love for him, and the presence of what he brought, whether among a people or within an individual?

Is not his removing punishment from them by way of what is more fitting and more worthy?

[A wonderful benefit concerning lam kay and lam al-juhud]

Lam kay (the lam of purpose) and lam al-juhud (the lam of denial) are two particles that are followed by an implied "an" (that). However, lam kay is the lam of causation (lam al-'illah), so only a verb that serves as the cause of what follows it may occur after it. If that verb is negated, this does not remove it from being lam kay, as al-Saymari held, because the sense of causation remains in it. The difference between lam al-juhud and lam kay lies in six aspects:

The first: lam al-juhud is preceded by a negated being (kawn) with the condition of past time, whether it was or was not, not in the future. So you do not say ma akun li-azurak (I will not be in order to visit you). It is a temporal, defective (naqisah) verb, not a complete (tammah) one.

Nor does a adverb of place or a prepositional phrase (majrur) occur after its subject. You do not say ma kana Zayd 'indaka liyadhhaba (Zayd was not with you in order to go), nor amsi liyakhruja (yesterday in order to go out).

These are four differences.

What unveils for you the veil of meaning and brings you straight to the point is that the temporal kana denotes a past time, so it cannot be the cause of a future event, nor does it govern an object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlihi), nor a circumstantial accusative (hal), nor adverbs of place. Its governing of an adverb of time is open to question. This is what prevented the lam of causation from preceding it, or a prepositional phrase or adverb from following it.

As for the fifth difference between the two lams: the verb after lam al-juhud cannot have its subject other than a pronoun referring back to the subject of kana, because the verb after it is in the place of the predicate. So you do not say ma kana Zayd liyadhhaba 'Amr (as you say ya Zayd liyadhhab 'Amr or litadhhab anta), but you say ma kana liyadhhaba and ma kunta li-af'al.

The sixth difference: it is permissible to make "an" explicit after lam kay, but it is not permissible to make it explicit after lam al-juhud. This is because in their speech it became the negation of a future verb with sa- or sawfa, so lam al-juhud took its place, and nothing that does not occur after it appears after it. In this subtle point there is insight into benefits from the Book of Allah and a ladder to reflecting upon it, such as His words: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them.﴾ Here lam al-juhud is used, since it is a negation of an anticipated matter and a feared cause in the future. Then He said: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness.﴾ Here the active participle is used, which is not restricted to a time, since He intended the negation of the occurrence of punishment upon those who seek forgiveness in general, without restriction to past or future. Similarly: ﴿Your Lord would not destroy the towns﴾ and then: ﴿We would not be destroyers of the towns.﴾ So observe this verse in light of the other, and you will find it so: it is lam al-'aqibah or lam al-sayrurah (the lam of consequence or of becoming).

As for lam al-'aqibah, which they call lam al-sayrurah, as in: ﴿so that they might become for them an enemy﴾, it is in reality lam kay, but it is connected to the predicate for the purpose of the one spoken of and his intention. Yet it is connected to the intention of the doer of the act in reality, who is Allah, Glorified and Exalted; that is, Allah did that so that it would be such and such. Likewise their saying: "He frees (a slave) so that he dies" — he did not free him for the purpose of death, and the lam is not connected to the act; rather the meaning is that God decreed that he frees so that he dies. So it is connected to what is decreed and to the act of God.

Its parallel is: «Indeed I forget so that I may be reminded» [weak].

Whoever narrates it as «unassa» with the intensive form has unveiled the veil of meaning. I heard our shaykh Abu al-'Abbas Ibn Taymiyyah say: It is impossible for lam al-'aqibah to enter the act of God, for wherever it occurs in speech, it is due to the agent's ignorance of the consequence of his act, like the picking up of Moses by the family of Pharaoh, for they did not know its outcome; or due to the agent's inability to avert the consequence, as in: "Give birth for death and build for ruin."

As for the act of one from whom not an atom's weight is hidden, and who has power over all things, it is never anything but lam kay, which is the lam of causation. Such benefits, which are hardly found in books, require sitting with the shaykhs and scholars.

(Verifying the meaning of wilayah)

He said: Some of them mentioned that it is permissible for a person to say, "I am a believer (mu'min)," but not to say, "I am a friend of God (wali)." They distinguished between the two, for God the Exalted commanded whoever has manifested faith to be called a believer. He the Exalted said: ﴿And if you know them to be believers﴾, and the verse goes on.

He did not command whoever has manifested that to be called a friend (wali). They did not distinguish between them, for God has described the friend (wali) with the attribute of the believer. He said: ﴿And they were not its friends. Its friends are only the God-fearing﴾. This is the attribute of the believer. Then it is not permissible for a person to describe himself as a friend, and likewise the believer. Moreover, he is only a friend through his devotion to the obedience of God and his standing in it, just like the believer.

I say: This is the argument of those who prohibit a person's saying, "I am a believer," without an exception (istithna'), just as he does not say, "I am a friend." As for one who distinguished between them, he answered that he cannot know that he is a friend, because wilayah is nearness to God, Mighty and Majestic. So the friend of God is the one who is near to Him and specially attached to Him.

Wala' (nearness) linguistically means closeness. It has signs and evidences, causes, conditions and requirements, and it has impediments, afflictions and severing factors. So a servant does not know whether he is a friend of God or not. As for faith, it is that one believes in God the Exalted, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the meeting with Him, and commits to performing His obligations and abandoning His prohibitions. This a person can know about himself; indeed, others can know it about him too.

What appears to me from this is that the wilayah of God the Exalted is of two kinds: general and specific. The general is the wilayah of every believer: whoever is a believer and God-fearing has a share of wilayah, in proportion to his faith and piety. There is nothing to prevent him, in this general wilayah, from saying, "I am a friend, God willing," just as he says, "I am a believer, God willing."

The specific wilayah: if a person knows of himself that he upholds all of God's rights, prefers Him over everything else in all his states, such that the pleasures and love of God have become his concern and the object of his thoughts, morning and evening his aim is the good pleasure of his Lord, even if people are displeased, then when such a person says, "I am a friend of God," he is truthful.

The verifiers (muhaqqiqun) in the matter of "I am a believer" have gone to exactly this same distinction. They said: He may say, "I have believed in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the meeting with Him," but he should not say, "I am a believer," because his saying "I am a believer" conveys complete, absolute faith, belonging to one who fulfills the obligations and abstains from the prohibitions. This is unlike his saying, "I have believed in God." So reflect on it.

"Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar, 'Atiyyah, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "al-Muka' is whistling, and al-Tasdiyah is clapping."

Likewise the people of language (ahl al-lughah) said: al-Muka' is whistling. It is said: makā, yamkū, muka' (mukā'), when a person joins his hands and then whistles into them. From this comes the expression makata ist al-dābbah (the rear of the animal made a sound), when wind came out of it with a noise. For this reason it is formed on the pattern of sounds, like rughā' (the bellowing of a camel), 'uwā' (the howling of a dog), and thughā' (the bleating of a sheep).

Ibn al-Sikkit said: All sounds are formed with a ḍammah (u-vowel), except for two words: al-nidā' (calling) and al-ghinā' (singing).

As for al-tasdiyah, in the language it is clapping. It is said: ṣadā, yuṣaddī, taṣdiyah, when a person claps with his hands.

Ḥassān ibn Thābit, reproaching the polytheists for their whistling and clapping, said:

"When the angels stood, you rose up,
Your prayer was clapping and whistling."

Similarly, Muslims may engage in such things during obligatory and voluntary prayers while whistling and clapping.

Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) said: "The Quraysh used to circumambulate the House naked, whistling and clapping."

Mujahid said: "They would obstruct the Prophet (ﷺ) during the circumambulation, whistling and clapping, confusing his prayer and his circumambulation," and something similar is reported from Muqatil.

There is no doubt that they did this and that.

Those who draw near to Allah through whistling and clapping resemble the first type, and their brethren who mix these into the prayer, remembrance and recitation of the people of prayer resemble the second type.

Ibn 'Arafah and Ibn al-Anbari said: al-muka' and al-tasdiyah are not prayer, but Allah the Exalted informed that they made in place of the prayer that they were commanded to perform the muka' and tasdiyah, so great burdens were imposed upon them for this. This is like your saying: "I visited him, but he made my visiting his reward (ṣilah)," meaning he set aversion in place of the reward.

The point is: those who clap and whistle in a flute, a reed pipe, or similar instruments share a resemblance to these people. Even if it is merely an outward resemblance, they bear a share of blame in proportion to their imitation of them, even if they do not imitate them in all of their whistling and clapping. Allah the Glorified did not prescribe clapping for men at a time of need during prayer when something befalls them; rather, they were ordered to turn away from it to glorification (tasbīḥ), lest they imitate women. So how much more so when they do it without need, and combine with it various types of sins in speech and action?

(Fa'ida) — A Benefit

Hostile disbelievers who seize the property of Muslims and then embrace Islam keep that property and it is not returned to the Muslims, because it was taken in the cause of God, and their rewards for it rest with God, in exchange for what the disbelievers destroyed of their blood and property. Martyrs are not held liable, and if the killer of a martyr embraces Islam, he is not obligated to pay blood-money (diyah) or expiation (kaffarah), according to the mass-transmitted Sunnah (al-sunnah al-mutawatirah) and the consensus of the Muslims. A group embraced Islam during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, and he knew who had killed them, such as Wahshi ibn Harb, the slayer of Hamzah, and the slayer of al-Nu'man ibn Qawqal, and others. The Prophet ﷺ did not demand anything from anyone, acting upon His saying: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they desist, what has passed will be forgiven them﴾ [al-Anfal: 38].

Likewise the apostates: Tulayhah al-Asadi embraced Islam after his apostasy, and he had killed Ukkashah ibn Mihsan, yet Abu Bakr, Umar, and the rest of the Companions did not hold him liable for blood-money or expiation.

Likewise, all who were killed by apostates, and the combatants who returned to Islam, the Muslims did not hold them liable for anything of that.

On this there is a dispute within the school of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad. A group of their followers support the liability (al-daman), and many of the later followers of Ahmad assume that this is the apparent position of his school, and that the non-liability is the view of Abu Bakr 'Abd al-'Aziz; but it is not known that Ahmad explicitly stated the view of Abu Bakr. Also, the people of apostasy and the combatants are not liable for what they destroyed of souls and property, like the original disbelieving enemies, and there is a dispute on that within the school of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad. The correct position regarding them is that held by the majority, which is the school of Malik, Abu Hanifah, and others.

Likewise, the rebels who hold a interpretation (al-baghun al-mutawwilun) from among the People of the Qiblah, like those who fought at the Battle of the Camel and at Siffin, are not held liable for what some of them destroyed of others in the fighting, and this is the preferred view among the followers of Ahmad.

al-Zuhri said: "The strife (al-fitnah) occurred while the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ were present in large numbers, and they unanimously agreed that every blood or wound inflicted through interpretation of the Qur'an is void (hadar), they placed them in the station of the Age of Ignorance." That is: since they were interpreting, they were placed in the station of the people of Ignorance, even if they were mistaken in the interpretation, like the disbelievers and apostates. Liability falls only on one who knew that it was not lawful for him to kill, like the two fighting groups who fought out of tribal partisanship (asabiyyah).

Each of them knew that it was fighting out of partisanship, not for a right; so each group is liable for what it destroyed of the other. Concerning this the saying of God the Exalted was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, retaliation is prescribed for you regarding those murdered: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female﴾ [al-Baqarah: 178].

As for the highwaymen (al-muharibun), the brigands who know that what they did is forbidden, they are liable; and if they repent before being overpowered, the penalties of God (hudud Allah) fall from them, just as they fall from the disbelievers who resist and then embrace Islam before being overpowered.

(Note)

Being afflicted by fitnah through love of forms is incompatible with one's religion being entirely for Allah. Rather, it diminishes the extent to which one's religion is for Allah, in proportion to the affliction of love that has befallen him.

It may even remove from its possessor anything of religion remaining for Allah. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah and religion is entirely for Allah.﴾

So He contrasts the existence of fitnah with the existence of religion being entirely for Allah. Each of the two negates the other.

Fitnah has been explained as shirk (associating partners with Allah).

Thus, whatever causes a fitnah in the hearts is either shirk or one of the causes of shirk.

It is a genus under which there are kinds of doubts (shubuhat) and desires (shahawat).

(Section)

The word "fitnah" in the Book of Allah the Exalted is used to mean a trial in which the one tested was not afflicted, but came through free of affliction. It is also used to mean a trial in which affliction did occur.

From the first sense is the saying of Allah the Exalted to Musa (peace be upon him): ﴿And We tested you with a [severe] testing﴾ [Ta-Ha: 40].

From the second sense is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah﴾ [al-Anfal: 39], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, into fitnah they have fallen﴾ [at-Tawbah: 49].

It is also applied to what encompasses both matters, like the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. Do people think that they will be left to say, "We believe," and they will not be tried? And We had already tried those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and will surely make evident the liars﴾ [al-Ankabut: 1-3].

And from it is the saying of Musa (peace be upon him): ﴿It is not but Your trial by which You send astray whom You will and guide whom You will﴾ [al-A'raf: 155]. That is, Your testing and Your trial: You send astray by it whoever falls into it, and You guide whoever is saved from it.

And fitnah is applied to something more general than that, like the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, your wealth and your children are only a fitnah﴾ [at-Taghabun: 15].

Muqatil said: "That is, a trial and a distraction from the Hereafter." Ibn Abbas said: "So do not obey them in disobedience to Allah the Exalted."

Al-Zajjaj said: Allah the Mighty and Majestic informed them that wealth and children are among the things by which people are tested. This is general to all children, for a person is tested through his child, since he may disobey Allah the Exalted because of him, consume the unlawful for his sake, and fall into grave sins, except whom Allah the Exalted protects.

What supports this is what is narrated: that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) "was delivering a khutbah when al-Hasan and al-Husayn (may Allah be pleased with them both) came, wearing two red shirts, stumbling. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) came down to them, took them, placed them in his lap on the minbar, and said: 'Allah has spoken the truth: ﴿Indeed, your wealth and your children are only a fitnah﴾ [at-Taghabun: 15].
