I saw these two boys and I could not be patient with them.'"

Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "None of you should say: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from fitnah,' for there is none among you but that he contains fitnah, because Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, your wealth and your children are only a fitnah﴾ [at-Taghabun: 15]. Whoever of you seeks refuge, let him seek refuge in Allah the Exalted from misguiding trials."

And from it is His saying: ﴿And We have made some of you a trial for others﴾ [al-Furqan: 20].

This is general to all creation: some are tested by others. The messengers are tested by those to whom they are sent, through their call to the truth, patience over their harm, and bearing hardships in conveying the messages of their Lord. Those to whom they are sent are tested by the messengers: will they obey them, support them, and believe them, or will they disbelieve in them, reject them, and fight them? The scholars are tested by the ignorant: will they teach them, advise them, and be patient in teaching, advising, and guiding them, along with what that entails? The ignorant are tested by the scholars: will they obey them and be guided by them? Rulers are tested by subjects, and subjects by rulers; the rich are tested by the poor, and the poor by the rich; the weak by the strong, and the strong by the weak; masters by their followers, and followers by their masters; the owner by his slave, and the slave by him; a man by his wife, and a wife by him; men by women, and women by men; believers by disbelievers, and disbelievers by believers. Those who enjoin good are tested by those they enjoin, and those who are enjoined are tested by them. For this reason, the poor and weak believers, among the followers of the messengers, were a trial for their rich and leaders, who refrained from belief after recognising the truthfulness of the messengers, and said: ﴿Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 11]. These people.

And they said to Nuh (peace be upon him): ﴿Shall we believe you while the lowest have followed you?﴾ [ash-Shu'ara: 111].

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And thus We tested some of them by means of others, that they might say, "Is it these whom Allah has favoured among us?"﴾ [al-An'am: 53].

So when the noble, the leader, sees the poor, humble one has preceded him to faith and following the Messenger, he becomes proud and disdainful of submitting, lest he be like him, and says: "Shall I submit so that I and this lowly one are on equal footing?" There is no remedy for one who has been afflicted by fitnah like patience. If he is patient, the fitnah purifies him and removes his sins, just as the furnace separates the dross from gold and silver.

So fitnah is the furnace of hearts and the touchstone of faith, and by it the truthful is distinguished from the liar. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We had already tried those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and will surely make evident the liars﴾ [al-Ankabut: 3].

Thus fitnah divides people into truthful and liar, believer and hypocrite, good and wicked. Whoever is patient with it, it becomes mercy for him, and by his patience he is saved from a greater fitnah; whoever is not patient with it falls into a worse fitnah.

Fitnah is unavoidable in this world and the Hereafter, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Day they will be burned over the Fire: "Taste your trial. This is what you were seeking to hasten."﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 13-14].

The Fire is a fitnah for those who were not patient with the fitnah of this world. Allah the Exalted said regarding the tree of Zaqqum: ﴿Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers﴾ [as-Saffat: 63].

Qatadah said: When Allah the Exalted mentioned this tree, the wrongdoers were tempted by it, saying: "Is there in the Fire a tree, while the Fire consumes trees?" So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that emerges from the root of Hellfire﴾ [as-Saffat: 64].

He informed them that its nourishment is from the Fire, meaning it was nourished by fire.

Ibn Qutaybah said: The tree of Zaqqum may be a plant of fire, made of a substance the fire does not consume. Likewise the chains of the Fire, its shackles, its fetters, its scorpions and its serpents; if they were of what is known to us, they would not remain in the Fire. Allah has only guided us to the unseen in His presence through what is present to us, so the names agree in signification while the meanings differ. What is in Paradise of its fruit, its furnishings, its trees and all its implements is of the same kind.

The point is: this tree is a fitnah for them in this world through their denial of it, and a fitnah for them in the Hereafter through their eating from it.

Likewise, His informing that the number of angels appointed over the Fire is nineteen was a fitnah for the disbelievers. The enemy of Allah, Abu Jahl, said: "Does Muhammad frighten you with nineteen, while you are the multitude? Can not each hundred of you overpower one of them, and then you come out of the Fire?" Abu al-Asad said: "O assembly of Quraysh, when the Day of Resurrection comes, I will walk before you on the Path, and I will push ten of them into the Fire with my right shoulder and nine with my left shoulder, and we will proceed and enter Paradise."

So the mention of this number was a fitnah for them in this world, and a fitnah for them on the Day of Resurrection.

The disbeliever is tested by the believer in this world, just as the believer is tested by him. For this reason the believers asked their Lord not to make them a trial for the disbelievers, as the monotheists (al-hunafa') said: ﴿Upon You we have relied, and to You we have turned back, and to You is the destination. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the disbelieving people﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 4-5].

And the companions of Musa (peace be upon him) said: ﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people﴾ [Yunus: 85].

Mujahid said: The meaning is, do not punish us at their hands nor with a punishment from You, so that they say: "If these were upon the truth, this would not have befallen them."

Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning: do not let them prevail over us, lest they think they are upon the truth and be tempted by that.

Al-Farra' said: Do not let the disbelievers prevail over us, lest they see that they are upon the truth and I am upon falsehood.

Muqatil said: Do not restrict our provision and extend it to them, for that would be a trial for them.

Allah the Exalted has informed that He tested each of the two groups by the other, saying: ﴿And thus We tested some of them by means of others, that they might say, "Is it these whom Allah has favoured among us?"﴾ Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾

The point is: Allah the Exalted tested the people of desires through beautiful forms, and tested those (the other group) through them. Each of the two kinds is a fitnah for the other. Whoever among them is patient with that trial is saved from what is greater than it, and whoever is struck by that trial falls into what is worse than it. If he remedies that through repentance and sincere advice, well; otherwise he is on the path of those who perish. For this reason the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) said: "I have left after me no fitnah more harmful to men than women," or as he said.

The servant in this abode is tested by his desires, his commanding self, his misleading and alluring devil, his companions, and what he sees and witnesses, which his patience cannot withstand. Added to that are weak faith and certainty, a weak heart, bitterness of patience, tasting the sweetness of what is immediate, the soul's inclination to the flower of this worldly life, and the reward being deferred to another abode other than this one in which he was created and raised. So he is obligated to abandon his present, witnessed desire for an unseen matter he was commanded to believe in:

By Allah, were it not that Allah makes His servant happy through His grace, and Allah is more merciful to the servant,

When faith, on a day, has firmly settled in his heart, upon these afflictions, though the matter is greater,

And the soul did not obey him in abandoning a desire, out of fear of a fire whose embers blaze,

And he did not fear one day the standing before his God, in which He judges with justice, for He does not wrong.

(Section)

Fitnah is of two kinds: fitnah of doubts (shubuhat), which is the greater of the two, and fitnah of desires (shahawat).

Both may combine in the servant, and he may be afflicted by only one of them.

The fitnah of doubts arises from weakness of insight and little knowledge, especially when corrupt intention and the presence of whim accompany it. Then is the great fitnah and the greatest calamity. Say what you will about one who has an evil intention, whose judgment is governed by whim rather than guidance, with weak insight and little knowledge of what Allah sent His Messenger with. He is among those of whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They follow only assumption and what souls desire﴾ [an-Najm: 23].

Allah the Exalted has informed that following whim misguides from the way of Allah, saying: ﴿O David, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth, so judge between the people in truth and do not follow desire, lest it lead you astray from the way of Allah. Indeed, those who stray from the way of Allah will have a severe punishment for having forgotten the Day of Account﴾ [Sad: 26].

The outcome of this fitnah is disbelief and hypocrisy; it is the fitnah of the hypocrites and the fitnah of the people of innovation, according to the levels of their innovations. All of them innovated only from the fitnah of doubts, in which truth was confused for them with falsehood, and guidance with misguidance.

This fitnah is not escaped except by devoting oneself to following the Messenger and making him the judge in the minor and major matters of religion, outward and inward, beliefs and actions, realities and laws. One receives from him the realities of faith and the laws of Islam, and what Allah affirms of attributes, acts and names, and what He negates of them, just as one receives from him the obligation of the prayers, their times and their numbers, the measures of the thresholds of zakat and its recipients, the obligation of wudu' and ghusl from janabah, and fasting in Ramadan. One does not make him a messenger in some matters of religion and not in others; rather he is a messenger in everything the community needs in knowledge and action, and one receives only from him and takes only from him. Guidance revolves entirely around his sayings and actions, and whatever departs from them is misguidance. When one fixes his heart upon this, turns away from anything else, and weighs everything by what the Messenger brought: if it agrees with it, he accepts it, not because the speaker said it, but because it agrees with the message; and if it contradicts it, he rejects it, even if whoever said it was anyone. This is what saves him from the fitnah of doubts. If he misses this, he is struck by its fitnah in proportion to what he has missed of it.

This fitnah arises sometimes from corrupt understanding, sometimes from false transmission, sometimes from a established truth that was hidden from the man so he did not attain it, and sometimes from a corrupt aim and a followed whim. It stems from blindness of insight and corruption of will.

As for the second kind of fitnah, the fitnah of desires:

Allah the Exalted combined mention of the two fitnahs in His saying: ﴿Like those before you who were stronger than you in power and more abundant in wealth and children. They enjoyed their share, and you have enjoyed your share as those before you enjoyed their share, and you have indulged in vain discourse as they indulged﴾ [at-Tawbah: 69].

That is, they enjoyed their portion of the world and its desires; khalaq is the apportioned share. Then He said: "and you have indulged as those who indulged," this indulgence being in falsehood, which is doubts.

In this verse He pointed to what corrupts hearts and religions: enjoying one's share and indulging in falsehood, because the corruption of religion is either by believing falsehood and speaking it, or by acting contrary to sound knowledge.

The first is innovation and what is akin to it; the second is the wickedness of deeds.

The first is corruption from the side of doubts, the second from the side of desires.

For this reason the salaf used to say: "Beware of two kinds of people: the man of whim whose whim has afflicted him, and the man of worldliness whose worldliness has blinded him."

They used to say: "Beware of the fitnah of the wicked scholar and the ignorant worshipper, for their fitnah is a fitnah for everyone who is tested."

The root of every fitnah is preferring opinion over the Sharia and whim over reason.

The first is the root of the fitnah of doubt, and the second the root of the fitnah of desire.

The fitnah of doubts is repelled by certainty, and the fitnah of desires is repelled by patience. For this reason Allah made leadership in religion dependent on these two matters, saying: ﴿And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and were certain of Our signs﴾ [as-Sajdah: 24].

This shows that leadership in religion is attained through patience and certainty.

He also combined them in His saying: ﴿And advise one another to truth and advise one another to patience﴾ [al-Asr: 3].

So advising one another to truth repels doubts, and advising one another to patience restrains from desires. He also combined them in His saying:

﴿And mention Our servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, possessors of strength and insight﴾ [Sad: 45].

"Strength" refers to powers and resolve for the sake of Allah, and "insight" to perceptions regarding the command of Allah. The expressions of the salaf revolve around this.

(Section)

When the servant is safe from the fitnah of doubts and desires, he attains the two greatest sought-after goals, by which is his happiness, success and perfection: guidance and mercy.

Allah said concerning Musa and his servant:

﴿So they found a servant from among Our servants, whom We had given mercy from Us and taught him knowledge from Our presence﴾ [al-Kahf: 65].

He combined mercy and knowledge for him, which is like the saying of the people of the cave: ﴿Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance﴾ [al-Kahf: 10].

Indeed, rushd (right guidance) is knowledge of what benefits and acting upon it. Rushd and huda, when mentioned separately, each includes the other; when mentioned together, each is distinct. Huda is knowledge of the truth; rushd is acting upon it. Their opposites are ghayy (error) and following whim.

(Fasl)

As for the lam in His words: ﴿that whoever perishes might perish by clear proof, and whoever lives might live by clear proof﴾, it is the lam of causation (lam al-ta'lil) in its proper sense, for it is mentioned in explaining His wisdom in gathering His allies and His enemies without prior appointment, and in granting victory to His allies despite their fewness, their weakness, and the smallness of their number and equipment, over the people of might, numbers, and iron weapons, such that no human would imagine they could prevail over them. That was one of the greatest signs of the Lord, the Glorified, by which He confirmed His Messenger and His Book, so that whoever chose for himself disbelief and obstinacy after it would perish by clear proof, and so he would have no argument against Allah, and whoever came to life through faith in Allah and His Messenger would live by clear proof, so that no doubt or uncertainty would remain with him. This is among the greatest of wisdoms. A parallel to this is His words: ﴿It is nothing but a reminder and a clear Qur'an, to warn whoever is alive and that the word may be justified against the disbelievers﴾.

(Section: Among the signs of love by which it is known)

Among them is frequent mention of the Beloved, and being constantly occupied with remembering Him and speaking of Him. Whoever loves something mentions it much, in his heart and on his tongue. For this reason Allah, glorified is He, commanded His servants to remember Him in all circumstances, and He commanded them to remember Him at the time they are most afraid. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who have believed, when you encounter a company, stand firm and remember Allah much that you may be successful.﴾

Lovers take pride in mentioning their beloveds at times of fear and at the meeting of enemies, as one of them said:

"I remember you while the spear-tips pass between us, and the straight spears have already drunk from us."

Another said:

"I remembered you while the lances were like the ropes of a well in the chest of a dark steed, so I wished to kiss the swords, for they flashed like the lightning of your smiling mouth."

In some divine reports it is said: "My servant, the truest of My servants, is the one who remembers Me while he is meeting his adversary." So the sign of sincere love is remembering the Beloved in times of desire and of dread. One of the lovers said about his beloved:

"The good and the evil remind me of you, and that which I fear and that which I hope for and that which I anticipate."

Among the remembrance that indicates the sincerity of love is that the Beloved's mention precedes the lover's heart and tongue at the first waking from his sleep, and that His mention be the last thing he sleeps upon, as one of them said:

"The last thing in every drowsing is you, and the first thing at the time of my stirring."

Remembrance of the Beloved does not come from a firmly established forgetfulness, for His mention is present potentially in the lover's soul; but because the place is narrow for it, things come upon him that veil the mention, and when the passing thing departs, the remembrance returns as it was. The highest kind of remembering the Beloved is that the lover restrains his tongue upon His remembrance, then restrains his heart upon his tongue, then restrains his heart and tongue upon witnessing the One remembered. Just as remembrance is a fruit of love, love is also a fruit of remembrance; each of them produces the other, and the seed of love is watered only with the water of remembrance. The best remembrance is that which issues from love.

Section: And among its signs is submission to the Beloved's command and preferring it over the lover's own desire; indeed the will of the lover and the Beloved becomes one. This is the true unity, not the unity that the brethren of the Christians among the heretics speak of.

There is no unity except in the will. This unity is the sign of sincere love, such that the will of the Beloved and the lover is one. Whoever has a will that opposes the will of his beloved is not a sincere lover; rather, he is one who wants from the beloved, not one who wants the beloved. If he wants him, he does not want what the beloved wants. The lovers are of three kinds: among them are those who want from the Beloved, among them those who want the Beloved, and among them those who want what the Beloved wants along with wanting the Beloved. This is the highest rank of lovers, and renunciation of this kind is the highest kind of renunciation, for it is only attained through perfect following of the Beloved's Messenger.

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: If you should love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ So He, glorified is He, made following His Messenger a cause of their being loved by Him. That the servant be loved by Allah is higher than that he be a lover of Allah. The matter is not that you love Allah, but that Allah loves you. Obedience to the Beloved is the sign of His love, as it has been said:

"You disobey God while claiming to love Him; this is a wondrous impossibility by analogy.
If your love were sincere, you would obey Him, for the lover is obedient to the one he loves."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 8, verse 46:

To proceed: Allah, glorified is He, made patience a steed that never stumbles, a sword that never turns dull, an army that is never defeated, and a fortress that is never destroyed or breached. Patience and victory are two full brothers. Victory comes with patience, relief comes with distress, and ease comes with hardship. Patience is more helpful to its possessor than men, without equipment or numbers. Its place in success is like the place of the head in the body. The Faithful, the Truthful, has guaranteed to His people in His firm Book that He will give them their reward without reckoning. He informed them that He is with them through His guidance, His mighty help, and His clear victory, and He said, Exalted is He: ﴿And be patient. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.﴾

So the patient won, by this companionship, the good of this world and the Hereafter, and they gained both through blessings, outward and inward. Allah, glorified is He, made leadership in religion depend on patience and certainty, and He said, Exalted is He, and by this statement the rightly guided were guided: ﴿And We made among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and used to be certain of Our signs.﴾

He informed that patience is good for its people, emphasizing it with an oath, and He said, Exalted is He: ﴿And if you are patient, it is better for the patient.﴾ He also informed that with patience and piety, the plot of the enemy will not harm, even if the enemy has power. He said, Exalted is He: ﴿But if you are patient and fear Allah, their plot will not harm you at all. Indeed, Allah is encompassing of what they do.﴾

He informed about His prophet Yusuf, the truthful, that his patience, piety, and righteousness brought him to a station of honor and empowerment. He said: ﴿Indeed, whoever fears Allah and is patient, indeed Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost.﴾ He linked success to patience and piety, and the believers understood this from Him, as He said, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, be patient, endure with one another, stay stationed at your posts, and fear Allah that you may succeed.﴾

He informed about His love for His people, and in this is the greatest encouragement for those who seek it. He said, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah loves the patient.﴾ He also gave good news to the patient of three things, each of which is better than what the people of this world compete for. He said, Exalted is He: ﴿And give good tidings to the patient, who, when disaster strikes them, say, "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return." Those upon them are blessings from their Lord and mercy, and those are the rightly guided.﴾

He instructed His servants to seek help through patience and prayer in the calamities of this world and religion. He said, Exalted is He: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed, it is difficult except for the humble.﴾ He made the attainment of Paradise and salvation from the Fire attainable only by the patient. He said, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, I have rewarded them today for what they patiently endured; indeed, they are the triumphant.﴾ He informed that desire for His reward and turning away from this world and its adornment is attained only by those of patience and the believers. He said, Exalted is He: ﴿And those who were given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds, but none receives it except the patient."﴾ He, Exalted is He, informed that repelling evil with what is better makes the wrongdoer like a close friend. He said: ﴿The good and the evil are not equal. Repel [evil] with that which is better, and thereupon the one between you and him is hostility as if he were a devoted friend.﴾ And this quality is not received except by those who are patient, and none receives it except one of great fortune.

Allah, glorified is He, informed, emphasizing with an oath: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss, except for those who believe, do righteous deeds, advise each other to truth, and advise each other to patience.﴾

He divided His creation into two categories: the companions of the right and the companions of the left. He singled out the people of the right as those who advise each other to patience and compassion, and He singled out those of patience and gratitude for benefiting from His signs, as a distinction for them with this abundant share. He said in four verses of His Book: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for every patient, grateful person.﴾

He tied forgiveness and reward to righteous deeds and patience, and this is for the one whom it is made easy for. He said: ﴿Except for those who are patient and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness and great reward.﴾

He informed that patience and forgiveness are among the resolute matters, whose merchants will never suffer loss. He said: ﴿And whoever is patient and forgives, indeed that is of the matters requiring determination.﴾ He commanded His Messenger to be patient for the sake of His judgment, and informed that his patience is only by Him, and by this all calamities become easy. He said: ﴿And be patient for the decision of your Lord, for indeed you are under Our eyes.﴾ And He said: ﴿And be patient, and your patience is not except through Allah. And do not grieve over them, and do not be in distress over what they plot. Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good.﴾

Patience is the believer's tethering-post, around which he roams and to which he returns. It is the shin upon which his faith stands, and his faith rests on nothing else. There is no faith for one who has no patience, and if he has some faith, it is a little faith in an extreme state of weakness. Its possessor is among those who worship Allah on the edge: if good befalls him, he is content with it, and if a trial befalls him, he turns over on his face, losing this world and the Hereafter, and gaining from them nothing but the losing bargain. Thus the best life that the fortunate attained was through their patience, and they ascended to the highest ranks through their gratitude. They traveled between the two wings of patience and gratitude toward the Gardens of Bliss. That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.

For he appeared to the polytheists when they set out for Badr, in the form of Suraqa ibn Malik, and said: "I am your protector against the Banu Kinana, lest they intend harm to your families and your offspring." When the enemy of Allah saw the hosts of Allah, the angels, sent down to support His Messenger, he fled from them and abandoned them, as Hassan said:

*He deceived them with delusion, then abandoned them; indeed the wicked one is a deceiver to whoever follows him.*

People have differed over the words of the enemy of Allah, ﴿Indeed I fear Allah﴾. Qatada and Ibn Ishaq said: "The enemy of Allah spoke truly in his words, ﴿Indeed I see what you do not see﴾, and lied in his words, ﴿Indeed I fear Allah﴾. By Allah, there was no fear of Allah in him, but he knew that they had no strength and no defence, so he led them on and abandoned them.

Such is the habit of the enemy of Allah with those who obey him."

Another group said: "He only feared the punishment of Allah, the Exalted, to befall him in this world, as the disbeliever and the wicked fear being killed or seized for their crime, not that he feared His punishment in the Hereafter." This is the more correct view, and this kind of fear does not imply faith or salvation.

Al-Kalbi said: "He feared that Jibril would seize him, and would then make known his state to them, so they would not obey him."

This is corrupt, for he only said this to them after he had fled and turned back on his heels. Unless he means that when the polytheists learned that the one who had protected them and led them on was Iblis, they would not obey him afterwards. But if that is what he meant, he has strayed far from the point and burdened the words with a meaning they do not bear.

Ata said: "I fear that Allah will destroy me along with those who are destroyed." This is fear of destruction in this world, and so it does not benefit him.

Al-Zajjaj and Ibn al-Anbari said: "He thought that the appointed time of which he had been granted respite had arrived."

Ibn al-Anbari added, saying: "He feared that the appointed time, at which his respite would end, had come, and that punishment would fall upon him. When he saw the angels, he feared that the time of respite had run out, so he said what he said out of concern for himself."

[Section: The appearance of Iblis in the form of Suraqa al-Kinani and his whispering to the Quraysh]

When they resolved to set out, they recalled the war that lay between them and the Banu Kinana. Iblis appeared to them in the form of Suraqa ibn Malik al-Mudlaji, who was one of the nobles of the Banu Kinana, and said to them: "No one among the people will overcome you today, and I am your protector against Kinana bringing you anything you dislike." So they went out, with Satan as their protector, never leaving them. When they drew up for battle and the enemy of Allah saw the host of Allah descending from the heavens, he fled and turned back on his heels. They said: "Where are you going, O Suraqa? Did you not say that you were a protector for us, and would not leave us?" He said: "Indeed I see what you do not see. Indeed I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment." He spoke truly in his words, "Indeed I see what you do not see," and lied in his words, "Indeed I fear Allah." It has also been said that his fear was for his own self, that he would perish along with them, and this is the more apparent view.

Al-Tabarani mentioned in his *al-Mu'jam al-Kabir*, from Rifa'a ibn Rafi', who said: "When Iblis saw what the angels were doing to the polytheists on the Day of Badr, he feared that the killing would reach him, so al-Harith ibn Hisham seized hold of him, thinking him to be Suraqa ibn Malik. He struck him in the chest and threw him down, then he fled until he cast himself into the sea. He raised his hands and said: 'O Allah, I ask You for Your respite for me.'" He feared that the killing would reach him. Then Abu Jahl ibn Hisham came forward and said: "O people! Let not the abandonment of Suraqa, who left you, defeat you, for he was in a pact with Muhammad. Let not the killing of Utba, Shayba and al-Walid dismay you, for they were hastened. By al-Lat and al-Uzza, we will not return until we bind them with ropes. None of you shall kill a man of theirs, but seize them alive until we make them know the evil of what they have done."

When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease saw the fewness of the party of Allah and the multitude of its enemies, they thought that victory came only through numbers, and said: ﴿These people's religion has deluded them﴾. Then Allah, glory be to Him, informed them that victory comes through reliance upon Him, not through multitude or numbers. Allah is the Mighty, who is not overcome, the Wise, who gives victory to whoever deserves it, even if he is weak. His might and His wisdom necessitated the victory of the party that relies upon Him.

When the enemy drew near and the two sides faced one another, "the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among the people and exhorted them, reminding them of what they would gain through patience and steadfastness: victory and swift triumph, and the reward of Allah that is yet to come. He informed them that Allah had made Paradise obligatory for whoever was martyred in His way. Then Umayr ibn al-Humam stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a Paradise whose breadth is the heavens and the earth?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Bakh, bakh!' The Prophet said: 'What makes you say bakh, bakh?' He said: 'No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, only the hope that I may be among its people.' He said: 'Indeed you are among its people.' So he took out some dates from his quiver and began to eat from them. Then he said: 'If I live long enough to eat these dates of mine, that would be a long life!' So he threw away what dates he had with him, then fought until he was killed. He was the first to be slain."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took a handful of pebbles and threw them at the faces of the enemy. He did not leave a single man among them without filling his eyes, and they were occupied with the dust in their eyes, while the Muslims were occupied with killing them. Allah revealed concerning this throwing to His Messenger: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw﴾ [al-Anfal: 17].

Ibn al-Anbari added, saying: "He feared that the appointed time, at which his respite would end, had come, and that punishment would fall upon him. When he saw the angels, he feared that the time of respite had run out, so he said what he said out of concern for himself."

[Section: The appearance of Iblis in the form of Suraqa al-Kinani and his whispering to the Quraysh]

When they resolved to set out, they recalled the war that lay between them and the Banu Kinana. Iblis appeared to them in the form of Suraqa ibn Malik al-Mudlaji, who was one of the nobles of the Banu Kinana, and said to them: "No one among the people will overcome you today, and I am your protector against Kinana bringing you anything you dislike." So they went out, with Satan as their protector, never leaving them. When they drew up for battle and the enemy of Allah saw the host of Allah descending from the heavens, he fled and turned back on his heels. They said: "Where are you going, O Suraqa? Did you not say that you were a protector for us, and would not leave us?" He said: "Indeed I see what you do not see. Indeed I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment." He spoke truly in his words, "Indeed I see what you do not see," and lied in his words, "Indeed I fear Allah." It has also been said that his fear was for his own self, that he would perish along with them, and this is the more apparent view.

Al-Tabarani mentioned in his *al-Mu'jam al-Kabir*, from Rifa'a ibn Rafi', who said: "When Iblis saw what the angels were doing to the polytheists on the Day of Badr, he feared that the killing would reach him, so al-Harith ibn Hisham seized hold of him, thinking him to be Suraqa ibn Malik. He struck him in the chest and threw him down, then he fled until he cast himself into the sea. He raised his hands and said: 'O Allah, I ask You for Your respite for me.'" He feared that the killing would reach him. Then Abu Jahl ibn Hisham came forward and said: "O people! Let not the abandonment of Suraqa, who left you, defeat you, for he was in a pact with Muhammad. Let not the killing of Utba, Shayba and al-Walid dismay you, for they were hastened. By al-Lat and al-Uzza, we will not return until we bind them with ropes. None of you shall kill a man of theirs, but seize them alive until we make them know the evil of what they have done."

When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease saw the fewness of the party of Allah and the multitude of its enemies, they thought that victory came only through numbers, and said: ﴿These people's religion has deluded them﴾. Then Allah, glory be to Him, informed them that victory comes through reliance upon Him, not through multitude or numbers. Allah is the Mighty, who is not overcome, the Wise, who gives victory to whoever deserves it, even if he is weak. His might and His wisdom necessitated the victory of the party that relies upon Him.

When the enemy drew near and the two sides faced one another, "the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among the people and exhorted them, reminding them of what they would gain through patience and steadfastness: victory and swift triumph, and the reward of Allah that is yet to come. He informed them that Allah had made Paradise obligatory for whoever was martyred in His way. Then Umayr ibn al-Humam stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a Paradise whose breadth is the heavens and the earth?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Bakh, bakh!' The Prophet said: 'What makes you say bakh, bakh?' He said: 'No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, only the hope that I may be among its people.' He said: 'Indeed you are among its people.' So he took out some dates from his quiver and began to eat from them. Then he said: 'If I live long enough to eat these dates of mine, that would be a long life!' So he threw away what dates he had with him, then fought until he was killed. He was the first to be slain."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took a handful of pebbles and threw them at the faces of the enemy. He did not leave a single man among them without filling his eyes, and they were occupied with the dust in their eyes, while the Muslims were occupied with killing them. Allah revealed concerning this throwing to His Messenger: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw﴾ [al-Anfal: 17].

[Section: Sins Remove Blessings]

Among the punishments of sins is that they remove blessings and bring down retributions. A blessing is never removed from a servant except because of a sin, and a retribution never descends upon him except because of a sin, as ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "No calamity descends except because of a sin, and it is not lifted except by repentance."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much.﴾ [al-Shūrā: 30]

And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That is because Allah never changes a blessing He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves.﴾ [al-Anfāl: 53]

So Allah informed that He does not change the blessings He has bestowed upon anyone until that person himself changes what is within himself. He changes obedience to Allah into disobedience to Him, gratitude into disbelief, and the causes of His pleasure into the causes of His wrath. When he changes, He changes [his circumstances] in return, as a fitting recompense, and your Lord is never unjust to the servants.

If he changes disobedience into obedience, Allah changes for him punishment into well-being and humiliation into honor.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when Allah wills for a people misfortune, there is no repelling it, and they have no protector besides Him.﴾ [al-Raʿd: 11]

In some divine narrations, from the Lord, blessed and exalted is He, He said: "By My might and My majesty, if a servant of Mine is in a state that I love, then moves from it to what I dislike, I will change for him what he loves into what he dislikes. And if a servant of Mine is in a state that I dislike, then moves from it to what I love, I will change for him what he dislikes into what he loves."

The poet has said well:

If you are in a blessing, then guard it,
for sins remove blessings.
Restrain it by obedience to the Lord of the servants,
for the Lord of the servants is swift in retribution.
Beware of injustice as much as you are able,
for the injustice done to people is grievous in its burden.
Travel with your heart among the people
so that you may see the traces of those who wronged.
Those are their dwellings after them,
witnesses against them, so do not doubt.
Nothing harmed them more
than injustice, which destroyed them.
How many gardens and palaces they left behind,
and other fortresses built over them.
They burned in the Blazing Fire, and the pleasures were lost,
and what they had attained became like a dream.

(Another section)

Sins remove blessings. Among their punishments is that they remove present blessings and cut off blessings that were coming. They remove what has been attained and prevent what was approaching. Allah's blessings are not preserved in their existence by anything like obedience to Him, nor is what is missing brought back by anything like obedience to Him. What is with Him cannot be obtained except through obedience to Him. Allah, glorified is He, has made for everything a cause and a blight: a cause that brings it, and a blight that nullifies it. He made the causes of His blessings that bring them obedience to Him, and their blights that prevent them disobedience to Him. So when He wills to preserve His blessing upon His servant, He inspires him to safeguard it through obedience to Him regarding it. And when He wills its removal from him, He forsakes him until he disobeys Him with it.

It is strange that a servant knows this by direct observation in himself and in others, and by hearing reports of what is hidden from him about those whose blessings Allah removed because of their sins, yet he persists in disobeying Allah. It is as if he is exempt from this general rule, or specially excluded from this universal principle. As if this matter befalls people but not him, and reaches creatures but not him. What ignorance is greater than this? And what wronging of the self is worse than this? Judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Great.

(Benefit)

Among the general hidden blights is that a servant is in a blessing that Allah has bestowed upon him and chosen for him, yet the servant becomes weary of it and seeks to move from it to what he imagines, due to his ignorance, to be better for him. His Lord, in His mercy, does not remove him from that blessing, and excuses him for his ignorance and poor choice for himself. Until, when he becomes narrow-hearted with that blessing, resentful of it, and disgusted with it, and his possession of it becomes firm, Allah strips it from him. Then when he moves to what he sought and sees the disparity between what he was in and what he has become, his anxiety and regret intensify and he seeks to return to what he was in. But when Allah wills good and right guidance for His servant, He makes him witness that what he is in is a blessing from Him upon him, and makes him content with it, and inspires him to thank Him for it. Then when his soul suggests to him to move away from it, he seeks guidance from his Lord as one ignorant of his own benefit and incapable of knowing it, entrusting the matter to Allah and asking Him for good choice for him.

Nothing harms a servant more than his weariness of the blessings of Allah, for he does not see them as blessings, does not thank Him for them, and does not rejoice in them. Rather, he resents them, complains about them, and considers them a calamity, though they are among the greatest of Allah's blessings upon him. Most people are enemies of Allah's blessings upon them, and they do not perceive that Allah has opened His blessings to them, while they strive to repel and reject them out of ignorance and injustice. How many a blessing has come to one of them while he strives with all his effort to repel it, and how many a blessing has reached him while he strives, by his wrongdoing and ignorance, to remove and eliminate it.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That is because Allah never changes a blessing He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves.﴾ And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves.﴾

There is no greater enemy to blessings than the soul of the servant itself. He is, together with his enemy, an accomplice against himself. His enemy casts fire into his blessings, and he blows upon it. It is he who enabled the throwing of the fire, then helped by blowing on it. When its blaze intensifies, he cries out from the burning, and his only recourse becomes blaming fate.

The poet said:

The one who is weak in judgment and wastes his opportunity,
until, when the matter has passed, he blames fate.

(Section)

Know that there are two matters with no third: one is that you are the one who stands in the path of your own benefits, the one who hinders the arrival of His grace to you, and you are an obstacle on the road of your own soul. This is the more common condition among creatures. For Allah, glorified is He, has decreed in His decree that what is with Him cannot be attained except through obedience to Him, and that Allah's blessings are not summoned without obedience to Him, nor are they lasted without thanking Him, nor are they blocked and prevented except by disobedience to Him. Likewise, if He bestows a blessing upon you and then strips it from you, He does not strip it out of stinginess, nor out of keeping it from you. Rather, you are the cause of its removal from you. For Allah does not change what is with a people until they change what is within themselves: ﴿That is because Allah never changes a blessing He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves, and indeed Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾ [al-Anfāl: 53]. So Allah's blessings are not removed except through disobedience to Him.

The poet said:

If you are in a blessing, then guard it,
for sins remove blessings.

So your ailment is from your own self, your affliction is from your own self. In reality, you are the one who has gone to extremes in enmity against yourself, and reached in opposing your soul what an enemy could not reach against you. As it is said:

What enemies can do to an ignorant man
is not what an ignorant man can do to his own soul.

It is strange that this is your conduct toward yourself, yet you complain about the Benefactor, the innocent who is beyond reproach. You accuse His decrees, contend with them, and blame them. You have wasted your opportunity and been negligent of your share, and your judgment has failed to recognize the causes of your happiness and to pursue them. Then you sit blaming fate with the tongue of your state and your speech. You are the one meant by the saying of the poet:

The one who is weak in judgment and wastes his opportunity,
until, when the matter has passed, he blames fate.

If you had perceived your own judgment, and known from where you were struck and from where you were afflicted, you could have made up for it. But the natural disposition has been corrupted, the heart has been turned upside down, and desire has extinguished the lamps of knowledge and faith within it. So you turned away from the One who is the root of your trial and calamity, and began complaining about every subtle or great favor that reached you from Him. When you complain of Him to His creatures, you are like what one of the gnostics ('ārifīn) said, when he saw a man complaining to another about what had befallen him and what had come upon him. He said: "O you, you complain of the One who has mercy on you to one who has no mercy on you."

If calamity comes to you, then bear it with patience,
the patience of the noble, for He is more merciful to you.
And if you complain to a son of Adam,
you are complaining of the Merciful to one who is not merciful.

When the servant knows the reality of the matter, and recognizes from where he was struck, by which route he was raided, and through which breach his goods were stolen and plundered, he will feel ashamed before himself, if not before Allah, to complain to any of His creatures, to accuse them of wronging him, or to see his calamity and affliction as coming from others. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much.﴾ [al-Shūrā: 30]. And He said: ﴿When a calamity struck you, though you had inflicted twice as much, you said, "From where is this?" Say, "It is from yourselves."﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 165]. And He said: ﴿Whatever good reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself.﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 79]

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 8, verse 60:

His saying: ﴿You will terrify thereby the enemy of Allah and your enemy, and others besides them whom you do not know. Allah knows them﴾

Regarding them there are two opinions. The first is that they are the jinn who support their enemies among mankind in fighting Allah and His Messenger. According to this view, the verse is explicit that "knowing" here means "recognizing," and it cannot be said that they knew the persons of those (jinn) while being ignorant of their enmity, as could be the case with humans.

The second opinion is that they are the hypocrites (munafiqun). According to this view, His saying ﴿you do not know them﴾ should be understood as referring to knowing their persons, not knowing their hypocrisy, because they (the Muslims) did know the hypocrisy of many of the hypocrites; they knew their hypocrisy and had no doubt about it. It is not permissible to deny them knowledge of what they actually know. Rather, what is denied is knowledge of the persons of this category, and this is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You do not know them; We know them﴾. So reflect upon it.

(Benefit)

My shaikh, may Allah have mercy on him, used to say: "Ahl al-dhimmah are not prevented from riding horses of the kind (that are noble), but if they ride the baradhin (ordinary draft horses) that have no adornment, and mules of this description, there is no prohibition. As for the donkey whose value reaches a level such that if one of them rides it, I have not seen any prohibition from the companions (of the madhhab) regarding it; perhaps they considered the category (of animal). And among the common sayings: riding a donkey is humiliation, and riding horses is honor," end of quote.

Al-Shafi'i said: "They should not ride a horse at all; they may only ride mules and donkeys."

His companions said: Ahl al-dhimmah are thus prevented from riding horses, since riding them carries great merit and honor, and they are the mounts of the mujahidin in the path of Allah, who protect the domain of Islam and defend the religion of Allah.

He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you can of power and of steeds of war, by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy﴾. So the tethering of horses was made for the purpose of terrifying the disbelievers. Therefore they may not be enabled to ride them, since that would involve terrifying the Muslims.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Horses have goodness tied to their foreheads until the Day of Resurrection." Reward, spoils, and the people of jihad are the people of horses and goodness, because they use horses in jihad; so they are most entitled to ride the mounts to which goodness is tied.

It has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, that horses were wild in the deserts, and the first to domesticate and ride them was Isma'il ibn Ibrahim; thus they are among the mounts of the sons of Isma'il, and with them they established the religion of the hanifiyyah, and upon them the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fought the enemies of Allah, and upon them the Companions conquered territories and supported Islam. So what do the enemies of Allah, upon whom humiliation has been decreed, have to do with riding them!

'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Do not honor them when Allah has humiliated them, and do not bring them close when He has distanced them."

[Section: The wisdom in distinguishing between horses and camels regarding zakat]

As for his saying: "He obligated zakat on five camels and waived it on thousands of horses," by the life of Allah, He obligated zakat on this category and not on that, as in Sunan Abi Dawud from the hadith of 'Asim ibn Damrah from 'Ali, may Allah honor his face, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have pardoned you regarding horses and slaves; so give the zakat of silver: from every forty dirhams, one dirham; there is nothing on one hundred and ninety; but when it reaches two hundred, then five dirhams are due in it." And Sufyan narrated it from Abu Ishaq from al-Harith from 'Ali.

Baqiyyah said: Abu Mu'adh al-Ansari narrated to me from al-Zuhri from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab from Abu Hurayrah, raising it (to the Prophet ﷺ): "I have pardoned you regarding the zakat of the jabhah, the kas'ah, and the nukhkhah." Baqiyyah said: The jabhah is horses, the kas'ah is mules and donkeys, and the nukhkhah is those raised in the houses. And in the book of 'Amr ibn Hazm: "There is no zakat on the jabhah and the kas'ah; the kas'ah is donkeys, and the jabhah is horses."

In the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet ﷺ: "There is no zakat upon a Muslim for his slave or his horse."

The difference between horses and camels is that horses are kept for other than what camels are kept for. Camels are kept for milk, breeding, eating, carrying loads, trade, and traveling on them from one land to another. As for horses, they were created for charging and retreating, pursuit and flight, establishing the religion, and waging jihad against its enemies.

The Lawgiver has a firm intent regarding their acquisition, preservation, and maintenance, and in encouraging souls to this by every means. For this reason He pardoned taking zakat from them, so that this would make souls more eager for what Allah and His Messenger love: acquiring them and tethering them. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you can of power and of steeds of war﴾.

So the tethering of horses belongs to the category of weapons and instruments of war. If a man had from them whatever amount but not for trade, there would be no zakat on him for it, unlike what is prepared for expenditure; for when a man owns a nisab of those, zakat is due on it. The Prophet ﷺ indicated this very point in his saying: "I have pardoned you regarding the zakat of horses and slaves; so give the zakat of silver." Do you not see how he distinguished between what is prepared for spending and what is prepared for raising the word of Allah, supporting His religion, and fighting His enemies? So it belongs to the category of swords, spears, and arrows, and the waiving of zakat on this category is among the excellences and perfection of the Shari'ah.

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary on Surah al-Anfal, verse 64:

That is: God alone is sufficient for you and for your followers, so you need no one else along with Him.

Here there are two possible readings. The first is that the wāw is conjunctive (ʿāṭifa) to "man" (مَن) over the kāf in the genitive. The conjunction of a noun onto a pronoun in the genitive without repeating the preposition is permissible according to the preferred school, and its evidence is abundant, and the objections that prohibit it are weak.

The second is that the wāw is the wāw of "with" (maʿa), and "man" is in the accusative position by way of conjunction to the place (al-mawḍiʿ), since "ḥasbuka" in meaning is "kāfīka" (your sufficient one). That is: God suffices you and suffices those who follow you, just as the Arabs say: "ḥasbuka wa-Zaydan dirham" (your sufficiency and Zayd's is a dirham). The poet said:

"When the battle rages and the staffs are split apart,
then you are sufficient, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, a keen-edged sword."

And this is the more sound of the two readings.

There is a third reading in it: that "man" is in the nominative position as the subject (mubtadaʾ), meaning: "And those of the believers who follow you, God is sufficient for them."

There is a fourth reading in it, and it is erroneous in terms of meaning: that "man" is in the nominative position, conjoined to the name of God, and the meaning would be: "God is sufficient for you, and your followers." Although some people have said this, it is pure error, and it is not permissible to interpret the verse this way. For "ḥasb" (sufficiency) and "kifāyah" (adequacy) belong to God alone, as do trust (tawakkul), piety (taqwā) and worship (ʿibādah). God Most High said: ﴿And if they intend to deceive you, then indeed God is sufficient for you. It is He who supported you with His help and with the believers﴾ [al-Anfal: 62].

So He distinguished between sufficiency and support: He made sufficiency for Himself alone, and made support His through His help and through His servants. God, glory be to Him, praised among His servants the people of monotheism and trust, in that they singled Him out for sufficiency, when He said: ﴿Those to whom people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them." But it increased them in faith, and they said, "God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs"﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 173].

They did not say, "God and His Messenger are sufficient for us." If this was their saying, and the Lord Most High praised them for it, then how could He say to His Messenger: "God and your followers are sufficient for you," while his followers have singled out the Lord Most High for sufficiency and did not associate His Messenger with Him in it? How then would He associate them and him in the sufficiency of His Messenger? This is among the most absurd impossibilities and the most false falsehoods. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿If only they had been content with what God and His Messenger gave them, and had said, "God is sufficient for us; God will give us of His bounty, and His Messenger too; to God we are turning in hope"﴾ [al-Tawbah: 59].

Consider how He made giving (īttāʾ) belong to God and His Messenger, as He said: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it﴾ [al-Ḥashr: 7].

And He made sufficiency belong to Him alone; He did not say, "they said: God and His Messenger are sufficient for us," but made it His exclusive right, as He said: ﴿Indeed, to God we turn in hope﴾.

And He did not say, "and to His Messenger," but made the turning in hope to Him alone, as He said: ﴿So when you are free, labour, and to your Lord turn your hope﴾ [al-Sharḥ: 7-8].

So turning in hope, trust, return (in repentance) and sufficiency belong to God alone, just as worship, piety and prostration belong to God alone, and vowing and swearing by oaths are only for God, glory be to Him and exalted.

A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿Is God not sufficient for His servant?﴾ [al-Zumar: 36].

So "ḥasb" means the sufficient one. He, glory be to Him and exalted, informed that He alone is sufficient for His servant; how then would He make His followers share with God in this sufficiency? The proofs demonstrating the invalidity of this corrupt interpretation are too many to be mentioned here.

The point is that according to one's following of the Messenger, there will be might, adequacy, and support, just as according to following him there will be guidance, success and salvation. God, glory be to Him, tied the happiness of both abodes to following him, and made the wretchedness of both abodes lie in opposing him. So for his followers there is guidance, security, success, might, adequacy, support, guardianship, strengthening, and a good life in this world and the Hereafter; and for his opponents there is humiliation, abasement, fear, misguidance, forsaking, and misery in this world and the Hereafter. The Prophet (ﷺ) swore that "none of you believes until he loves me more than his child, his parent and all people." God, glory be to Him, swore that whoever does not make him (the Messenger) judge in all that he and others dispute, then accepts his judgment without finding any discomfort in himself about what he decided, and submits to it completely and yields to it fully, does not believe. God Most High said: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 36].

So God, glory be to Him and exalted, cut off choice after His command and the command of His Messenger. It is not for a believer to choose anything after his command (ﷺ); rather, when he commands, his command is binding. Choice exists only in the saying of others when his command is obscure and that other is among the people of knowledge of him and of his Sunnah. With these conditions, the saying of another becomes permissible to follow, not obligatory to follow. No one is obliged to follow the saying of anyone other than him; at most, it is permissible for him to follow it, and if he leaves off taking the saying of another, he is not disobeying God and His Messenger. How far is this from one whom all accountable people are obliged to follow, whose opposition is forbidden to them, and who must leave every saying for his saying? No judgment is for anyone in his presence, no saying is for anyone in his presence, just as no legislation is for anyone in his presence. Every other than him is obeyed only in his saying when he commands what he commanded and forbids what he forbade. He was a pure conveyor and informant, not an originator and founder. Whoever originates sayings and establishes rules according to his own understanding and interpretation, it is not obligatory for the community to follow them, nor to adjudicate by them, until they are presented to what the Messenger brought. If they conform to it and agree with it and are testified to be sound, they are then accepted; if they oppose it, their rejection and discarding is obligatory; and if neither of the two matters becomes clear in them, they are held in suspension, and the best of their status is that it is permissible to judge and issue fatwas by them or to leave them. As for it being obligatory and fixed, no, by no means.

(Benefit)

Sufficiency and adequacy are in proportion to faith. God Most High said: ﴿O Prophet, God is sufficient for you and for the believers who follow you﴾ [al-Anfal: 64].

That is: God is sufficient for you and for your followers, i.e., He suffices you and suffices them. So His sufficiency for them is in proportion to their following of His Messenger, their submission to him, and their obedience to him. Whatever decreases of faith returns with the decrease of all that.

The doctrine of the People of the Sunnah and the Community is that faith increases and decreases.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 8, verse 67:

"The Prophet (ﷺ) consulted the Companions about the captives of Badr. Abu Bakr advised him to take ransom from them, which would give them strength against their enemy, and to release them, perhaps Allah would guide them to Islam. Umar said: 'No, by Allah, I do not see what Abu Bakr sees. Rather, I see that you should let us take them and strike off their necks, for these are the leaders of disbelief and its chieftains.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) inclined to what Abu Bakr said and did not incline to what Umar said. When the next day came, Umar approached and found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr weeping. He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what makes you and your companion weep? If I find a reason to weep I will weep, and if I do not find one, I will feign weeping because of your weeping.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I weep for what your companions proposed to me regarding taking the ransom. Their punishment was presented to me, nearer than this tree,' and Allah revealed: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he has inflicted slaughter upon the land.﴾

People have disputed which of the two opinions was more correct. One group preferred the statement of Umar on account of this hadith, and another group preferred the statement of Abu Bakr, for the following reasons: the matter settled upon it; it agreed with the prior decree from Allah permitting that to them; it agreed with mercy, which overcame wrath; the Prophet (ﷺ) likened him in this to Abraham and Jesus, and likened Umar to Noah and Moses; a great good resulted from the Islam of most of those captives; Muslims emerged from their loins; the strength that the Muslims gained through the ransom was achieved; the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) agreed with Abu Bakr first, and Allah agreed with him last, when the matter settled upon his opinion; and the perfection of the judgment of the Siddiq, for he saw what the ruling of Allah would ultimately settle upon, and he prioritized the side of mercy over the side of punishment.

They said: As for the weeping of the Prophet (ﷺ), it was out of mercy for the descent of punishment upon those who desired the goods of this world by it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not desire that, nor did Abu Bakr. Even if some of the Companions desired it, the trial would be general and would not afflict only those who desired it specifically, just as the army was defeated on the day of Hunayn by the statement of one of them: '(We will not be overcome today for lack of numbers),' and by the admiration of their multitude for whoever among them was impressed; the army was thus defeated through that trial and tribulation. Then the matter settled upon victory and triumph. And Allah knows best.

The Ansar asked his permission to leave the ransom of his uncle al-Abbas to them, but he said: 'Do not leave any of it, not a single dirham.'

He requested from Salamah ibn al-Akwa' a slave-girl whom Abu Bakr had given him as a spoil in one of his expeditions, and he gave her to him, and he sent her to Makkah, and with her he ransomed some Muslims. He also ransomed two Muslim men in exchange for a man from 'Uqayl. He returned the captives of Hawazin to them after the division, and he won over the hearts of the spoil-takers, so they gave it up for him; and for whoever did not give it up, he compensated each person with six camels. He killed 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt from among the captives, and he killed al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, because of the intensity of their enmity toward Allah and His Messenger.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Some of the captives had no wealth, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made their ransom that they teach the children of the Ansar writing." This indicates the permissibility of ransom through labour, just as it is permissible through wealth.

His practice was that whoever embraced Islam before capture was not enslaved, and he would enslave the captives of the Arabs as he enslaved others from the People of the Book. "He had a captive woman from them with 'Aishah, and he said: 'Free her, for she is from the descendants of Isma'il.'"

The early scholars differed regarding this prior decree. The majority of the exegetes, both from among the early generations and those after them, said: "Had it not been for a decree from Allah that preceded you, O people of Badr, recorded in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), that the spoils of war are lawful for you, He would have punished you."

Others said: "Had it not been for a Book from Allah that preceded, stating that He does not punish anyone except after the proof has been established, He would have punished you."

Others said: "Had it not been for a Book from Allah that preceded for the people of Badr, stating that they are forgiven, even if they did whatever they wished, He would have punished them."

And others said, and this is the correct view: "Had it not been for a Book from Allah that preceded, containing all of this, ﴿a great punishment would have touched you for what you took﴾. And Allah knows best."
